NARRATIVE: ON JULY 10, 2026, AT APPROXIMATELY 0600 HOURS, A CONSTRUCTION MANAGER ARRIVING AT CONSUMERS ENERGY'S ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION OBSERVED NATURAL GAS VENTING NEAR PLANT 1 AND NOTIFIED THE STATION SUPERVISOR. THE ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION IS LOCATED IN IRA TOWNSHIP, ST. CLAIR COUNTY, MICHIGAN.   A STATION MECHANIC RESPONDED TO THE SITE AND CLOSED VENT VALVE #704, STOPPING THE RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS INTO THE ATMOSPHERE. THE MECHANIC THEN CLOSED THE UNIT 1-2 SUCTION VALVE AND REOPENED THE VENT VALVE TO SAFELY RELIEVE THE REMAINING TRAPPED GAS WITHIN THE ISOLATED SECTION OF PIPING. ONCE THE GAS WAS FULLY CONTAINED, THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTION TO THE PLANT 1 MOTOR CONTROL CENTER (MCC) BREAKER WAS EVALUATED TO ENSURE NO GROUND FAULT EXISTED ON THE CIRCUIT AND VERIFIED THAT PLANT OPERATIONS COULD BE SAFELY RESUMED.   A TEAM WAS ASSEMBLED TO INVESTIGATE THE ROOT CAUSE AND CONTRIBUTING FACTORS THAT LED TO THIS EVENT. THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT ON JULY 9, 2026, AT APPROXIMATELY 1854 HOURS, THE STATION EXPERIENCED A LOSS OF COMMUNICATION WITH THE ALLEN-BRADLEY PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC), RESULTING IN THE OPENING OF THE PLANT 1(MCC) BREAKER AND THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT 1-2. THE STATION OPERATOR WAS CALLED OUT AND RESPONDED TO THE UNIT 1-2 EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN.    THE INVESTIGATION FURTHER DETERMINED THAT VERIFICATION OF CRITICAL VALVE POSITIONS FOLLOWING THE UNIT 1-2 EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN WAS NEITHER DOCUMENTED NOR COMPLETED IN ACCORDANCE WITH ESTABLISHED OPERATING PROCEDURES. AS A RESULT, THE POSITION OF VENT VALVE #704 AFTER THE SHUTDOWN COULD NOT BE CONFIRMED. ADDITIONALLY, THE STATION OPERATOR PLACED UNIT 1-2 IN PLANNED OUTAGE AFTER ALIGNMENT WITH GAS CONTROL DUE TO THE EXPECTATION THAT CONTINUED ALARM ACTIVITY ASSOCIATED WITH THE COMMUNICATION FAILURE WOULD GENERATE NUISANCE ALARMS AT GAS CONTROL. CONSEQUENTLY, SUBSEQUENT ABNORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS ASSOCIATED WITH UNIT 1-2 WERE NOT COMMUNICATED TO THE GAS CONTROLLER, INCLUDING INDICATIONS THAT A VENTING EVENT MAY HAVE BEEN OCCURRING AT THE STATION.  FOLLOWING THE OPENING OF THE MCC BREAKER, UNIT 1-2 CONTINUED TO OPERATE ON POWER SUPPLIED BY THE STATION’S UNINTERRUPTIBLE POWER SUPPLY (UPS) FOR APPROXIMATELY SIX HOURS. AT APPROXIMATELY 0157 HOURS ON JULY 10, 2026, THE UPS BATTERIES WERE DEPLETED, RESULTING IN A LOSS OF CONTROL POWER TO UNIT 1-2.   UPON THE LOSS OF CONTROL POWER, VENT VALVE #704 OPENED WHILE THE UNIT’S SUCTION AND DISCHARGE ISOLATION VALVES REMAINED IN THE OPEN POSITION, CREATING A FLOW PATH THAT ALLOWED NATURAL GAS TO VENT TO ATMOSPHERE.   THE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS TEAM IS FINALIZING ITS INVESTIGATION AND DEVELOPING CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TO IMPROVE PROCESSES, PROCEDURES AND OPERATIONAL SAFEGUARDS TO PREVENT RECURRENCE. THE FINAL INVESTIGATION RESULTS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION PLAN WILL BE DOCUMENTED UPON COMPLETION OF THE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS.

NAME: GOLDEN TRIANGLE STORAGE, LLC
NARRATIVE: PART H – NARRATIVE DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT ON JUNE 14, 2026, AT 15:30 HOURS (CST), SYLVESTER SILLER, REGULATORY MANAGER FOR GOLDEN TRIANGLE STORAGE, LLC (“GTS”), WAS NOTIFIED OF AN UNINTENTIONAL AIR EMISSIONS RELEASE. FROM GTS INVESTIGATIONS, A FOUR (4)-INCH BLOWDOWN VALVE ON DEHY TRAIN B, KNOWN AS VALVE BDV5403B, WAS OFF SET AND VENTING GAS TO THE BLOWDOWN HEADER.   GTS INCIDENT RESPONSE  UPON DISCOVERY BY ONSITE GTS OPERATIONS STAFF, THE UPSTREAM MANUAL VALVE WAS IMMEDIATELY CLOSED, THE FLOW SUBSIDED, AND THE SYSTEM CAME INTO BALANCE.  INITIAL NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE WITHIN THE HOUR OF REPORT TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER WITH PRELIMINARY ESTIMATES OF LOST GAS.  AFTER FURTHER ASSESSMENT OF THE OPERATIONAL TRENDS, IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT A 26-HOUR PERIOD OF VENTING STARTED ON JUNE 13, 2026, FROM ONE (1) INDIVIDUAL BLOWDOWN POINT, RESULTING IN A CUMULATIVE VENTING OF 12.3 MMSCF OF NATURAL GAS TO ATMOSPHERE.    REASONS FOR REPORTING UNDER 49 CFR §191.3(1)(III), AN INCIDENT IS DEFINED AS UNINTENTIONAL ESTIMATED GAS LOSS OF THREE (3) MILLION CUBIC FEET (SCF) OR MORE. THE REPORTED EVENT CAUSED THE VENTING OF STORED NATURAL GAS FROM THE SYSTEM THROUGH AN ENGINEERED BLOWDOWN SYSTEM THROUGH A NORMAL ELEVATED POINT OF DISCHARGE.  THERE WERE NO INCREASED SAFETY RISKS OR EXPOSURE TO THE PUBLIC, NO ONSITE INJURIES, OR EQUIPMENT DAMAGE. HOWEVER, THE RELEASE OF THE GAS THROUGH THE VENT (BLOWDOWN) SYSTEM WAS STILL UNINTENTIONAL AND THEREFORE CONSIDERED A GAS LOSS MEETING THE CRITERIA ABOVE FOR REQUIRED REPORTING.  INVESTIGATION INTO THE ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATIONS ELUCIDATED THAT THE VALVE INITIALLY FAULTED WEEKS PRIOR TO INCIDENT BUT REMAINED CLOSED UNTIL THE AFTERNOON OF JUNE 13, 2026. THERE WAS NO UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE FROM VALVE BDV5403B PRIOR TO JUNE 13, 2026, AS CONFIRMED BY OPERATIONAL TREND DATA. TROUBLESHOOTING OF THE ACTUAL VALVE AND NATURAL GAS SYSTEM REVEALED NO DAMAGE OR REQUIRED REPAIRS TO THE LINE. VALVE BDV5403B AND ITS ASSOCIATED ACTUATOR ARE PART OF THE STATIONS BLOWDOWN SYSTEM AS REQUIRED BY CFR 192.167(A)(2), WHERE A FAIL-OPEN CONFIGURATION IS THE STANDARD DESIGN CHOICE TO PROVIDE A SAFE AND ROBUST SYSTEM.    GTS CORRECTIVE ACTIONS LOGIC ON CONTROLLERS IS BEING MODIFIED TO BETTER IDENTIFY AND CAPTURE THIS TYPE OF FAILURE.  BALANCE NOTIFICATIONS WILL BE BUILT INTO THE SYSTEM FOR THE OPERATORS, ALONG WITH FURTHER TRAINING TO ENSURE UNDERSTANDING OF THE LINE PACK ADJUSTMENTS.  ADDITIONAL TOOLS ARE BEING ADDED FOR TRACKING EVENTS FOR IMBALANCE VISIBILITY, AS WELL AS ADJUSTMENTS TO SYSTEM OPERATING CONDITIONS IN ORDER TO TIGHTEN THE IDENTIFICATION AND CAPTURE OF THESE TYPES OF VENTING EVENTS GOING FORWARD.  CLOSING IN THE EVENT PHMSA REQUIRES ADDITIONAL INFORMATION TO THIS 30-DAY FOLLOW UP REPORT, PLEASE DO NOT HESITATE TO REACH OUT TO SYLVESTER SILLER AT SSILLER@CALICHESTORAGE.COM, OR AFTON STERLING, VP OF REHS, AT ASTERLING@CALICHESTORAGE.COM.

NAME: EQT MIDSTREAM COMPANY LLC
NARRATIVE: ON 5/28/2026, EQT WAS CONDUCTING MOWING OPERATIONS OUTSIDE THE CALLISTO CS FENCELINE, NEAR THE PAJUPG075 (FKA NIJUS021) AND PAJUPG081 (FKA NIJUS029) RIGHT-OF-WAY. WHILE MOWING, THE EQT OPERATOR (EMPLOYEE “EE” #1) WAS INJURED BY SUDDEN FIRE. THE EQT OPERATOR ESCAPED FURTHER INJURY BY REMOVING HIMSELF FROM THE SCENE AND SEEKING HELP INSIDE THE CALLISTO CS OFFICE. THE INJURED OPERATOR INFORMED EE #2 OF WHAT HAPPENED.  AFTER ASSESSING THAT HIMSELF AND NO OTHER EES OR PUBLIC WERE IN IMMEDIATE DANGER, EE #2 CALLED THE 9-1-1 EMERGENCY CALL CENTER AT ~12:21PM. ADDITIONALLY, EE #2 INSTRUCTED A CONTRACTOR WHO WAS PRESENT TO CONTACT THE INJURED EE #1’S SUPERVISOR, EE #3, AS WELL AS EE #2’S SUPERVISOR (EE #4).  AT ~12:26PM, EE #2 CALLED MIDSTREAM GAS CONTROL (MGC) TO REPORT A FIRE NEAR PIPELINE PAJUPG081, REQUESTING THE ISOLATION OF THE PIPELINE. EE #2 ADVISED MGC THAT AN EE HAD SUSTAINED BURN INJURIES TO HIS HAND, AND THAT FIRE/EMS WAS ENROUTE TO THE SITE. MGC CONTACTED THE PRODUCTION CONTROL CENTER (PCC) AND REQUESTED THAT THE UPSTREAM CLEMENTE MM BE SHUT-IN. ADDITIONALLY, MGC SHUT DOWN COMPRESSOR UNIT #4 DOWNSTREAM OF THE SITE.  AT ~12:28PM, EE #4 CONTACTED THE EQT HOTLINE AND WAS CONNECTED WITH EE #5 FROM EHS AT 12:32PM, WHOM HE MADE AWARE OF THE SITUATION. AT ~12:33PM, MGC NOTIFIED EE #6 FROM MIDSTREAM COMPLIANCE AND SUPERINTENDENT EE #3. EE #3 ADVISED PIPELINE OPERATORS AND SUPERVISORS TO HEAD TO THE SITE.  TWO OPERATIONS SUPERVISORS (EES # 7 AND 8) ARRIVED ON-SITE AT ~12:45PM, WITH EE #7 SERVING AS THE OPERATIONS COORDINATOR FOR THE EVENT. AT APPROXIMATELY THE SAME TIME, EMERGENCY RESPONDERS ARRIVED ON-SITE. EE #7 ASSESSED THE SITUATION, AND INSTRUCTED THE FIRE CHIEF TO STAGE THEIR EQUIPMENT, DEPLOY HOSES, AND AWAIT FURTHER INSTRUCTION. THE FIRE CHIEF CONFIRMED THAT NO SUPPRESSION ACTIVITIES WOULD BE INITIATED UNTIL AUTHORIZATION WAS GIVEN. EMS PERSONNEL WERE DIRECTED TO THE CALLISTO CS OFFICE TO CARE FOR THE INJURED EE.  AT ~12:55PM, EE #7, WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF EE #8, BEGAN TO COORDINATE ON-SITE EFFORTS TO ISOLATE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK, IN CONJUNCTION WITH MGC. EE #7 DIRECTED PIPELINE OPERATORS TO BEGIN CLOSING MULTIPLE VALVES ON PAJUPG081, PAJUPG075, AND PAJUPG086 (FKA NIJUS041) TO ISOLATE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF GAS. FACILITY OPERATORS INSIDE CALLISTO CS WERE INSTRUCTED TO CONFIGURE THE YARD SO THAT ANY PIPELINE BLOWDOWN OR STATION ESD BLOWDOWN WOULD OCCUR ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF THE STATION, OPPOSITE THE LOCATION OF THE LEAK. DURING THESE ACTIVITIES, MGC REMOTELY CLOSED THE HCA VALVE TO CLEMENTE MM AT ~1:00PM TO FURTHER ISOLATE THE SYSTEM. AT ~1:05PM, LIFE FLIGHT ARRIVED ON THE SCENE. THE FINAL VALVE WAS SHUT ON PAJUPG086 AT ~1:40PM.   FOLLOWING THE FINAL ISOLATION VALVE CLOSURE, EE #7 PERFORMED A FINAL EVALUATION OF THE SCENE FOR THE SAFE BLOWDOWN OF THE PIPELINE ASSETS. EE # 7 NOTED THAT WINDS WERE BLOWING SOUTHWARD, AWAY FROM THE LEAK SITE. WITH CONDITIONS BEING SAFE, THE BLOWDOWN OF PAJUPG075 AND PAJUPG081 COMMENCED AT THAT SOUTHERN END OF THE CALLISTO CS SITE.  EE #7 CONSULTED WITH THE FIRE CHIEF AND AUTHORIZED FIRE SUPPRESSION ACTIVITIES TO COMMENCE ONCE BOTH LINES WERE FULLY DEPRESSURIZED. AT ~1:58PM, BLOWDOWNS ON BOTH PIPELINES HAD COMPLETED. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE WITH WATER.  AT ~3:16PM, COMPLIANCE ON-CALL WAS CONTACTED TO CONFIRM THAT THE INJURED EE WAS ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL AS AN IN-PATIENT. WITH CONFIRMED DISCOVERY OF A REPORTABLE INCIDENT, COMPLIANCE’S EE #6 NOTIFIED THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER OF THE INCIDENT AT ~3:25PM (NRC# 1463661).  EQT IS WORKING WITH A 3RD PARTY TO DETERMINE AN APPARENT CAUSE AND WILL PROVIDE A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT UPON COMPLETION OF THE INVESTIGATION.

NAME: CAPROCK MIDSTREAM SOUTH TEXAS LLC
NARRATIVE: AT 6:23 P.M. ON DECEMBER 10, 2025, A CONTRACTOR WAS NOTIFIED OF A POSSIBLE PIPELINE INCIDENT BY A MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC. THE CONTRACTOR CALLED THE OPERATOR, AND THE OPERATOR CHECKED LINE PRESSURE IN SCADA TO INVESTIGATE LEAK REPORT. OPERATOR IDENTIFIED UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES BASED ON APPROXIMATE LOCATION REPORTED BY THE PUBLIC. AT 6:34 P.M., OPERATOR CONTACTED THE CONTROL ROOM AND INSTRUCTED THEM TO REMOTELY CLOSE THE UPSTREAM VALVE DUE TO A POTENTIAL LINE BREAK AND STARTED DRIVE DOWNSTREAM MANUAL VALVE LOCATION. CONTROL ROOM PERSONNEL EXECUTED THE COMMAND AND CONFIRMED THE UPSTREAM VALVE WAS SUCCESSFULLY CLOSED. FOLLOWING VALVE CLOSURE, LINE PRESSURE DROPPED SIGNIFICANTLY, AND UPSTREAM PRESSURE WAS CONTINUOUSLY MONITORED. AT 7:34 P.M., OPERATOR PERSONNEL CLOSED THE MANUAL DOWNSTREAM VALVE TO FURTHER ISOLATE THE AFFECTED SEGMENT. OPERATOR ARRIVED AT THE INCIDENT SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 8:00 P.M. TO CONDUCT A PRELIMINARY ON-SITE EVALUATION AND BEGIN PIPELINE REPAIRS. AT 9:01 P.M., THE OPERATOR DETERMINED THE EVENT MET THE PHMSA AND RAILROAD COMMISSION OF TEXAS (RRC) IMMEDIATE NOTICE REPORTING THRESHOLDS (CONFIRMED DISCOVERY) DUE TO AN UNINTENTIONAL LOSS EXCEEDING 3 MMCF. CREWS MOBILIZED TO THE SITE TO CUT OUT AND REPLACE FAILED SECTION OF PIPELINE. ON DECEMBER 16, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 7:00 P.M., REPAIRS WERE COMPLETED AND THE PIPELINE WAS PURGED. THE LINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON DECEMBER 17, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 5:00 A.M.  FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT, THE FAILED PIPE SEGMENT WAS REMOVED AND SENT TO BAKER RISK FOR A METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS. THE FINAL REPORT IS EXPECTED BY THE END OF JANUARY, AND A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED WITH INFORMATION ON THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT.  2/3/2026 SUPPLEMENTAL - THE METALLURGICAL LAB REPORT FROM BAKER RISK WAS RECEIVED ON 1/21/2026. IT WAS DETERMINED EXTERNAL CORROSION WAS THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE. THE FOLLOWING SUMMARIZES THE CONCLUSIONS OF THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS REPORT:  1. THE PIPELINE WAS DAMAGED BY PITTING CORROSION.  2. THE PITTING CORROSION WAS LOCATED IN THE VICINITY OF THE 6 O’CLOCK POSITION ON THE PIPELINE.  3. THE PITTING CORROSION AREAS COINCIDED WITH THE LONGITUDINAL WELD SEAM STARTING ~36 INCHES DOWNSTREAM OF GIRTH WELD 12460 OVER A LENGTH OF ~84 INCHES.  4. THE WELD SEAM WAS PREFERENTIALLY ATTACKED WITHIN THE PITTED AREA.  5. THE RUPTURE INITIATED DUE TO WALL LOSS AT THE INITIATION SITE.  6. ONCE INITIATED, THE RUPTURE PROPAGATED BY DUCTILE OVERLOAD FAILURE.  7. THE PIPELINE RUPTURE FOLLOWED THE WELD SEAM IN THE JOINT BETWEEN GIRTH WELD 12460 AND GIRTH WELD 12470.  8. THE RUPTURE PROPAGATED IN A DUCTILE MANNER BOTH UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM FROM THE ORIGIN, TERMINATING ~ 4-FEET UPSTREAM OF GIRTH WELD 12460 AND JUST BEYOND GIRTH WELD 12470 ON THE DOWNSTREAM END.  9. THE ILI DATA IS GENERALLY CONSISTENT WITH THE PRESENT OBSERVATIONS AND MEASUREMENTS BUT UNDERESTIMATED THE SEVERITY OF THE PITTING. AT LEAST 56% WALL LOSS WAS PHYSICALLY MEASURED, WHEREAS THE ILI DATA ESTIMATED A MAXIMUM LOSS OF 39%.  NOTE: CAPROCK ACQUIRED THIS PIPELINE ON OCTOBER 1, 2025, AND IMMEDIATELY INITIATED A 5-WEEK REMEDIATION PROJECT (10/15/2025-11/20/2025) BASED ON THE RESULTS OF THE PREVIOUS OWNERS ILI RUN IN OCTOBER 2024.  AS A CORRECTIVE ACTION, CAPROCK HAS SCHEDULED ANOTHER ILI RUN ON THIS PIPELINE FOR THE WEEK OF FEBRUARY 9TH, 2026, AND WILL REVIEW AND ADDRESS DEFECTS OR ANOMALIES IN ACCORDANCE WITH 49 CFR 192.485(A)-(B).

NAME: NATIONAL FUEL GAS SUPPLY CORP
NARRATIVE: NATIONAL FUEL GAS SUPPLY CORPORATION (“NATIONAL FUEL”) IS REPORTING THIS NATURAL GAS INCIDENT AS A RESULT OF AN UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE OF GAS, WHICH RESULTED IN PROPERTY DAMAGE WITH ESTIMATED COSTS IN EXCESS OF THE APPLICABLE $145,400 THRESHOLD OUTLINED IN 49 C.F.R. § 191.3(1)(II) AND OCCURRING ON NATIONAL FUEL’S F1S PIPELINE IN THE TOWN OF LIMESTONE, CATTARAUGUS COUNTY, NY (“LINE F1S”). ON SUNDAY, JUNE 1, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 12:11PM, NATIONAL FUEL GAS CONTROL OPERATIONS CENTER RECEIVED AN ALARM DUE TO A PRESSURE DROP ON LINE F1S. AT APPROXIMATELY 12:14PM, THE PRESSURE DROP TRIGGERED A COMPRESSOR UNIT SHUTDOWN AT LIMESTONE COMPRESSOR STATION, WHICH ISOLATED THE COMPRESSOR STATION FROM LINE F1S. NATIONAL FUEL PROMPTLY MOBILIZED OPERATIONS TO INVESTIGATE. AT APPROXIMATELY 1:06PM, NATIONAL FUEL ARRIVED AT LIMESTONE COMPRESSOR STATION TO BEGIN THE INVESTIGATION INTO THE CAUSE OF THE ALARM, AND, ALTHOUGH A POTENTIAL SOURCE OF THE ALARM WAS NOT YET DISCOVERED, AS A PRECAUTIONARY ACTION, CLOSED VALVE CPC113 AT LIMESTONE STATION, WHICH IS IMMEDIATELY UPSTREAM OF LINE F1S. AT APPROXIMATELY 1:36PM, THE DOWNSTREAM VALVE ON LINE F1S (VALVE RHC111) WAS CLOSED TO ISOLATE LINE F1S. OUT OF AN ABUNDANCE OF CAUTION, AT APPROXIMATELY 2:46PM, NATIONAL FUEL NOTIFIED THE NRC OF A POTENTIAL RUPTURE. AFTER LINE F1S WAS ISOLATED, NATIONAL FUEL PATROLLED LINE F1S, AND, AT APPROXIMATELY 3:16PM, CONFIRMED A RUPTURE ON LINE F1S NEAR THE CROSSING OF RICE BROOK WITHIN ALLEGANY STATE PARK (GPS COORDINATES 42.0603, -78.69133). UPON EXCAVATING AND REMOVING THE RUPTURED SECTION OF LINE F1S, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE RUPTURE OCCURRED ALONG THE LONGITUDINAL SEAM OF AN APPROXIMATELY 50-FOOT JOINT OF PIPE AND ARRESTED 2-3 INCHES BEYOND THE GIRTH WELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. THE LONGITUDINAL SEAM WAS ORIENTED AT THE 6:00 O’CLOCK PIPE POSITION. THE RICE BROOK FLOWED ABOVE LINE F1S THROUGH TWO PARALLEL CORRUGATED METAL CULVERT PIPES, WHICH WERE DAMAGED AS A RESULT OF THE RUPTURE. THE FLOW OF RICE BROOK WAS TEMPORARILY DISRUPTED, BUT LATER RE-ESTABLISHED WITH MINIMAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS. LABORATORY ROOT CAUSE FAILURE ANALYSIS OF THE RUPTURED SECTION OF LINE F1S DETERMINED THE ROOT CAUSE WAS INTERNAL SELECTED SEAM WELD CORROSION (SSWC), INITIATING IN A SAG BEND AT A LOW POINT IN LINE F1S. THE LAB REPORT STATED THAT THE LOW POINT WOULD LIKELY COLLECT WATER AND OTHER POTENTIAL CONTAMINANTS FROM THE SERVICE FLUID, WHICH WOULD AID THE PROGRESS OF INTERNAL SSWC DUE TO LINE F1S'S SEAM HAVING BEEN INSTALLED AT THE 6:00 O'CLOCK ORIENTATION. LINE F1S WAS REPAIRED BY REPLACING APPROXIMATELY 60 FEET OF 6-INCH OD, 0.280-INCH WALL, GRADE X-52 STEEL PIPE WHICH WAS PRESSURE TESTED TO >1.5 X MAOP. NO INJURIES OR FATALITIES RESULTED FROM THE RUPTURE.

NAME: HARVEST MIDSTREAM COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON MAY 19, 2025, HARVEST INITIATED A ROUTINE FOAM PIGGING OPERATION ON THE PGGS SYSTEM AT APPROXIMATELY 11:00 AM AS PART OF STANDARD MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES. THE PIG WAS LAUNCHED WITHOUT INCIDENT; HOWEVER, PRESSURE IN THE PG-02 SEGMENT BEGAN TO RISE UNEXPECTEDLY LATER THAT AFTERNOON. THIS SEGMENT IS EQUIPPED WITH A 6-INCH PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (PRV) AND EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN VALVE (ESDV-1), MONITORED BY PRESSURE TRANSMITTER PT-201.     DURING THE INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE PIG ARRIVED SIGNIFICANTLY EARLIER THAN ANTICIPATED. THE TRAVEL TIME HAD BEEN PROJECTED USING SCADA FLOW DATA. THE PIG WAS EXPECTED TO TAKE UP TO TWO DAYS TO REACH ITS DESTINATION BUT COMPLETED THE RUN WITHIN A FEW HOURS. THIS UNANTICIPATED ARRIVAL LED TO CONDENSATE ACCUMULATION IN THE LINE, WHICH TRAVELED INTO THE ACTUATOR SUPPLY TUBING OF ESDV-1, CONTRIBUTING TO VALVE MALFUNCTION.     AT 5:14 PM, PT-201 REGISTERED A PRESSURE OF 526 PSI. THE HOUSTON CONTROL ROOM DETECTED THE TREND AND CONTACTED PIPELINE OPERATOR, WHO ADVISED THAT THE FOAM PIG WAS LIKELY STILL IN TRANSIT. HE INFORMED THE CONTROLLER THAT THE VALVE HAD PRESSURE RELIEF CAPABILITY AND INSTRUCTED THEM TO RESET THE VALVE IF NECESSARY AND NOTIFY HIM IF PRESSURE EXCEEDED 600 PSI.     AS PRESSURE CONTINUED TO RISE, PIPELINE OPERATOR INITIATED MANUAL SHUT-IN COORDINATION WITH THE HILCORP PLATFORM. AT 5:54 PM, PRESSURE REACHED 550 PSI AND ESDV-1 RECEIVED A CLOSE COMMAND, SHUTTING THE VALVE AS DESIGNED. HOWEVER, CONDENSATE ACCUMULATION IN THE REGULATOR AND ACTUATOR TUBING SUBSEQUENTLY PREVENTED THE VALVE FROM REOPENING.     THE CONTROL ROOM ISSUED MULTIPLE RESET COMMANDS TO ESDV-1 VIA SCADA, BUT THE VALVE REMAINED IN AN 'ERROR' STATE AND FAILED TO REOPEN. AT 6:37 PM, PRESSURE REACHED THE MAOP OF 606.2 PSI, PROMPTING THE CONTROLLER TO ESCALATE THE SITUATION TO OPERATIONS CONTROLS DIRECTOR, FOREMAN, AND PIPELINE OPERATOR.     BY 6:43 PM, SCADA ENGINEER WAS CONTACTED FOR SUPPORT. HE DETERMINED THAT THE ISSUE WAS NOT DUE TO A SCADA MALFUNCTION BUT WAS LIKELY CAUSED BY CONDENSATE IN THE REGULATOR AND ACTUATOR TUBING, WHICH PREVENTED THE VALVE FROM RECEIVING SUFFICIENT ACTUATION PRESSURE. AT 6:50 PM, PRESSURE PEAKED AT 620.9 PSI, EXCEEDING MAOP BUT REMAINING BELOW 110%, AND THE PRV ACTIVATED TO RELIEVE PRESSURE. THE PRV VENTED NATURAL GAS TO ATMOSPHERE FOR APPROXIMATELY 22 MINUTES.     AT 6:57 PM, FLOW THROUGH PG-02 DROPPED TO ZERO. AT 7:00 PM, A MANUAL CLOSE COMMAND WAS ISSUED TO ESDV-1, AND A PERMISSIVE SIGNAL WAS RECEIVED. PIPELINE OPERATORS AGREED TO KEEP THE VALVE CLOSED AND CONDUCT A STAND-UP PRESSURE TEST TO CONFIRM PIPELINE INTEGRITY.     THE TEST BEGAN AT 7:18 PM, WITH PT-201 READING 594.5 PSI. BY 8:01 PM, PRESSURE HAD STABILIZED AT 594.0 PSI. ALTHOUGH THE LINE WAS DEEMED SAFE TO RESTART, REPEATED ATTEMPTS TO REOPEN ESDV-1 WERE UNSUCCESSFUL.     AT 10:19 PM, PIPELINE OPERATOR AND I&E TECHNICIAN DECIDED TO KEEP THE SYSTEM SHUT-IN OVERNIGHT. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS IDENTIFIED AS A LIQUID-FILLED REGULATOR AND ACTUATOR TUBING, WHICH PREVENTED PROPER VALVE ACTUATION. PLANS WERE MADE TO ACCESS THE SITE THE FOLLOWING MORNING AND REPLACE THE AFFECTED COMPONENTS.

NAME: MISSISSIPPI HUB, LLC
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: AT 20:52 CDT ON 4/12/2025, AN 8-INCH PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (PRV) ATTACHED TO A 42-INCH HEADER AT THE MISSISSIPPI HUB UNGSF AND COMPRESSOR STATION WAS EJECTED DUE TO A RUPTURE OF THE PIPE SPOOL BELOW THE VALVE. AS A RESULT OF THE EVENT, THE ON-SITE OPERATIONS CONTROLLER EXPERIENCED A LOSS OF COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE SCADA SYSTEM. HOWEVER, THE STATION ESD SYSTEM FUNCTIONED AS DESIGNED AND SHUT IN THE FACILITY AUTOMATICALLY. THE FACILITY WAS IN THE PROCESS OF PREPARING TO WITHDRAW GAS FROM STORAGE WHEN THE EVENT OCCURRED.       THE ON-SITE OPERATOR WAS JOINED BY OTHER LOCAL EMPLOYEES AND BEGAN INVESTIGATING THE SOURCE OF THE FAILURE WHEN THE EJECTED PRV WAS DISCOVERED. THE PRV WAS LOCATED BETWEEN THE GAS HEATERS AND SEPARATORS DOWNSTREAM OF THE PRESSURE REGULATORS FOR THE COMINGLED GAS STREAM WHICH WAS NOT WITHIN THE UNGSF DEMARCATION. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE EXTENT OF PHYSICAL DAMAGE AND CORRECTIONS TO COMMUNICATIONS COULD NOT BE FULLY EVALUATED UNTIL DAYLIGHT, BUT THERE WAS NO CONCERN FOR THE SAFETY OF EMPLOYEES OR THE PUBLIC. THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, IGNITION OF THE GAS, EVACUATIONS, ROAD CLOSURES, OR MEDIA INQUIRIES.     THE FOLLOWING MORNING, PERSONNEL DETERMINED THE PRV HAD BEEN EJECTED VERTICALLY AND THROUGH A CABLE TRAY, RESULTING IN MULTIPLE DAMAGED CABLES. ONCE THE PRELIMINARY EXTENT OF THE DAMAGE HAD BEEN ASSESSED, IT WAS DETERMINED THE FACILITY WOULD BE SHUT IN WHILE REPAIRS WERE MADE. THE EVENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC AT 11:09 CDT ON 4/13/2025 SINCE REPAIRS COULD HAVE EXCEEDED $145,400 AND WE DETERMINED AT THAT TIME THAT THE EVENT RESULTED IN THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF AN UNGSF.     THE REPAIR WAS COMPLETED ON 4/16/2025, AND COMMUNICATIONS FOR THE FACILITY WERE RESTORED, ALLOWING THE FACILITY TO BE PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE ON 4/18/2025. THE FAILED PIPE UNDERWENT METALLURGICAL EXAMINATION, AND A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS WAS UNDERTAKEN TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE.     THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS DETERMINED THE PIPE SPOOL FAILURE WAS THE RESULT OF AN EXTERNAL OVERLOAD OF THE ASSEMBLY CREATED BY A PRESSURE RELEASE EVENT. THE PRESSURE RELEASE CAUSED A DOWNWARD FORCE AND BENDING MOMENT, TRIGGERING BUCKLING INSTABILITY JUST BELOW THE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE.    THE COMPONENTS OF THE ASSEMBLY ABOVE THE BUCKLE ROTATED NEARLY 45° FROM VERTICAL BEFORE A PARTING FAILURE OCCURRED.     A BULGE WAS PROGRESSIVELY GENERATED AS THE STRUCTURE BENT OVER, DISSIPATING SIGNIFICANT ENERGY. MICROGRAPHS SHOW THAT THE MATERIAL EXHIBITED SIGNIFICANT PLASTIC FLOW BEFORE FAILURE.     THE OVERALL PLASTIC BEHAVIOR OF THE MATERIAL LOCAL TO THE BULGE WAS CONSISTENT WITH MECHANICAL TESTING RESULTS. MECHANICAL TESTING SHOWS AN ELONGATION OF 32% TO 36% AND A REDUCTION IN AREA OF 66% TO 72%. SUBSIZE CHARPY V-NOTCH TEST SPECIMENS (5 MM X 10 MM) RETURNED AN AVERAGE TOUGHNESS OF 98 FT-LBS  AT 72°F(CONVERTED TO FULL SCALE).    THE FINAL FRACTURE INITIATION WAS CAUSED BY SHEAR OVERLOAD AT THE BUCKLE BULGE TIP ON THE OD.    NO SIGNS OF PREEXISTING ID OR OD CRACKS, DAMAGE, CORROSION, OR OTHER STRESS RISERS WERE FOUND. NO EVIDENCE EXISTED THAT PRIOR DAMAGE WEAKENED THE BUCKLING RESISTANCE OF THE STRUCTURE.     A FINITE ELEMENT ANALYSIS OF THE PIPE ASSEMBLY WAS UNDERTAKEN TO SUPPORT THE CONCLUSION THE PIPE SPOOL FAILURE WAS THE RESULT OF AN EXTERNAL OVERLOAD OF THE ASSEMBLY CREATED BY A PRESSURE RELEASE EVENT. THE PLASTIC COLLAPSE OVERLOAD IS CONSISTENT WITH THE FEA ENGINEERING ANALYSIS RESULTS.

NAME: UGI ENERGY SERVICES
NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 20, 2025, COMPRESSOR #2 WAS PLACED IN MAINTENANCE MODE FOR TROUBLESHOOTING AN ESD VENT VALVE STATUS ISSUE. LOOSE TERMINALS IN THE ACTUATOR CONTROL BOARD WERE IDENTIFIED AND REPAIRED. HOWEVER, MAINTENANCE MODE WAS ACCIDENTALLY LEFT ACTIVE OVERNIGHT.    THE MAINTENANCE MODE SHOULD HAVE TRIGGERED LOCAL ALARMS AND SMS NOTIFICATIONS AT 2, 12, AND 24 HOURS, BUT SMS ALERTS FAILED TO GENERATE. OPERATORS MISSED THE MAINTENANCE STATUS ON LOCAL SCADA DISPLAYS THE MORNING OF MARCH 21.    AT 12:24 ON MARCH 21, COMPRESSOR #2 SUCTION AND DISCHARGE BLOCK VALVES UNEXPECTEDLY CLOSED. NORMALLY THIS WOULD TRIGGER UNIT SHUTDOWN, BUT MAINTENANCE MODE BLOCKED ALL SHUTDOWN SIGNALS, FORCING THE COMPRESSOR TO RUN WITH CLOSED VALVES UNTIL 13:05 WHEN OPERATORS RECEIVED A LOSS OF RUN STATUS ALARM.    PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT 13:14 AND ASSESSED DAMAGE. DURING INSPECTION, A SMALL OIL FIRE WAS DETECTED BY THE SAFETY SYSTEM, CAUSING STATION ESD AT 13:23. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE.    POST-INCIDENT SCADA ANALYSIS REVEALED BOTH VALVES OPENED WITHOUT COMMAND AFTER THE COMPRESSOR STOPPED. THE ENGINE CONTROL PANEL INDICATED SHUTDOWN DUE TO MECHANICAL OVERLOAD.    THE VALVE CLOSURE CAUSED CATASTROPHIC MECHANICAL FAILURE REQUIRING COMPLETE REPLACEMENT OF FRAME, CRANKCASE, CRANKSHAFT, CYLINDERS, AND ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. THE MAINTENANCE MODE CAPABILITY HAS BEEN ELIMINATED FROM STATION PLC PROGRAMMING.    ROOT CAUSE WAS IDENTIFIED AS MALFUNCTION IN VALVE CONTROL CIRCUITRY, HARDWARE, WIRING, AND CONNECTIONS BETWEEN PLC AND VALVE ACTUATORS. DUE TO THE INTERMITTENT NATURE, SPECIFIC COMPONENT ISOLATION WAS IMPOSSIBLE DURING ONLINE OPERATION. INVESTIGATION ELIMINATED PLC PROGRAMMING AND HARDWARE, NARROWING THE FAULT TO PHYSICAL CONNECTIONS INCLUDING I/O BOARDS, CABINET CONNECTIONS, AND FIELD WIRING. HISTORICAL REVIEW REVEALED SIMILAR VALVE CLOSURES PREVIOUSLY MISDIAGNOSED AS PNEUMATIC ISSUES.    PRIOR TO RESTART, ALL PLC I/O BOARDS FOR BLOCK VALVE CONTROL WERE REPLACED, WIRING CONTINUITY VERIFIED, AND ACTUATOR TERMINATIONS INSPECTED. SINCE RETURNING TO SERVICE APRIL 29, 2025, NO UNEXPECTED VALVE POSITION CHANGES OCCURRED. COMBINED WITH REMOVAL OF PROBLEMATIC MAINTENANCE FUNCTIONS AND NEW MAINTENANCE MODE SAFEGUARDS, WE ARE CONFIDENT THE ROOT CAUSE IS RESOLVED AND SIMILAR ELECTRICAL FAILURES WOULD NOT RESULT IN THE SAME INCIDENT TYPE.

NAME: BLUEWATER GAS STORAGE, LLC
NARRATIVE: RE: OMO RD COMPRESSOR STATION INCIDENT  NRC INCIDENT REPORT #1413461 & FOLLOW UP #1413594    ON OCTOBER 5, 2024 AT APPROXIMATELY 3:09 AM, EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) VENT VALVES (BDV 9010) AND (BDV 9011) OPENED BECAUSE OF A LOSS OF POWER GAS PRESSURE USED TO HOLD THE ESD VALVES CLOSED.  PIPELINE ISOLATION (SDV-9001) WAS ALSO OPEN, RESULTING IN A GAS RELEASE OF ~5.2 MMSCF TO ATMOSPHERE.   THE LOSS OF POWER GAS WAS CAUSED BY OF A COMBINATION OF AN ISOLATION OF THE POWER GAS HEADER AND A LEAKING REGULATOR IN THE POWER GAS SYSTEM.  ON OCTOBER 3, 2024, AT 10:56 A.M., THE FUEL GAS SUPPLY VALVE (SDV 9008) TRIPPED / CLOSED DUE TO HIGH PRESSURE (>475 PSIG).  THE HIGH PRESSURE WAS CAUSED BY DAYTIME HEATING AND THERMAL EXPANSION OF THE GAS IN THE FUEL GAS SYSTEM. THE OMO ROAD COMPRESSOR STATION WAS SHUTDOWN AT THE TIME, MINIMIZING FUEL GAS USE AND CAUSING FUEL GAS HEADER PRESSURE TO FLUCTUATE WITH AMBIENT TEMPERATURE. IN ADDITION TO ITS PRIMARY FUNCTION TO SUPPLY FUEL TO THE NATURAL GAS FIRED ENGINES USED TO DRIVE THE GAS COMPRESSORS AT THE STATION, THE FUEL GAS SYSTEM ALSO PROVIDES POWER GAS TO THE POWER GAS HEADER.  TYPICALLY, POWER GAS PRESSURE IS HIGH ENOUGH THAT THE GAS PRESSURE OVERCOMES THE SPRING TENSION USED TO OPEN THE BLOWDOWN VALVES IN THE EVENT OF AN ESD.   FOLLOWING THE OVERPRESSURE CONDITION, SDV 9008 WAS NOT REOPENED BECAUSE THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS IDLE AND THE NEED FOR FUEL GAS WAS MINIMAL.  WITH SDV 9008 CLOSED AND THE POWER GAS HEADER ISOLATED, A LEAKING REGULATOR ON BDV 9011 EVENTUALLY BLED OFF ENOUGH PRESSURE FROM THE POWER GAS HEADER TO ALLOW BDV 9010 AND BDV 9011 TO FAIL OPEN AS DESIGNED. THE LEAKING REGULATOR WAS IDENTIFIED FOLLOWING THE RELEASE ON OCTOBER 5, 2024 AND REPAIRED ON OCTOBER 17, 2024.    CORRECTIVE ACTION:  BLUEWATER WILL IMPLEMENT CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TO PRECLUDE REPETITION OF THE INCIDENT, MINIMIZE THE AMOUNT OF VENTED GAS, AND IMPROVE REPORTING TIMELINESS.  1. UPDATE PROCEDURES TO AVOID THE ISOLATION OF THE POWER GAS HEADER:  A. OPTION 1: SDV 9008 (FUEL GAS SUPPLY) WILL BE OPEN DURING NORMAL AND STAND BY OPERATIONS  B. OPTION 2: (TBD) VB-9071 CHANGED TO 'NORMALLY OPEN' TO PROVIDE AN UNINTERRUPTED SUPPLY TO THE POWER GAS HEADER  2. CONTROL LOGIC AT THE SITE ALLOWED FOR THE PIPELINE VALVE (SUPPLY GAS) TO REMAIN OPEN WHEN THE VENT VALVES BDV 9010 AND BDV 9011 WERE OPEN.   A. BLUEWATER HAS UPDATED LOGIC AT THE FACILITY, IF A VENT VALVE IS IN ANY POSITION OTHER THAN "CLOSED" THE PIPELINE VALVE FEEDING THE FACILITY (SDV 9001) WILL CLOSE.  3. AT SOME TIME PRIOR TO 11:27 AM, POTENTIALLY OVERNIGHT, PRESSURE BUILT BETWEEN THE BARRIERS INSTALLED AT 1,507 FEET MD AND 2,424 FEET MD. AT 11:27 AM, THE WORKOVER CREWS BEGAN TO RELEASE THE RETRIEVABLE PACKER INSTALLED AT 1,507 FEET MD TO RETRIEVE IT FROM THE WELL. AS THE PACKER WAS RELEASED, THE FORCE FROM THE BUILT-UP PRESSURE PUSHED THE WORKSTRING AND RETRIEVABLE PACKER OUT OF THE WELLBORE IN APPROXIMATELY 3 TO 5 SECONDS. THE GAS THAT BUILT UP BETWEEN THE TWO DOWNHOLE BARRIERS WAS RELEASED. IN LESS THAN THIRTY SECONDS, THE ONSITE CREWS SECURED THE WELL WITH MULTIPLE BARRIERS (MASTER VALVE AND BLOWOUT PREVENTER ELEMENTS). THE WORKSTRING CONTACTED THE ELECTRONICS OF AN OFFSET WELL, WHICH SHUT DOWN IN THE INTENDED FAILSAFE CONDITION AND PROVIDED THE INITIAL INDICATIONS OF AN INCIDENT TO THE CONTROL ROOM VIA THE SCADA SYSTEM. THE SURFACE PIPING OF THREE OFFSET WELLS WAS CONTACTED AND THEN TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE UNTIL ASSESSMENTS CONFIRMED THE DAMAGE WAS ONLY COSMETIC.    THE WELL WORK PROCEDURE SPECIFIED TO EQUALIZE PRESSURE ACROSS THE RETRIEVABLE PACKER INSTALLED AT 1,507 FEET MD PRIOR TO RELEASING IT. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROCEDURAL STEP IS TO MITIGATE THE POSSIBILITY OF A FAILURE OF THE ISOLATING BARRIER INSTALLED AT 2,424 FEET MD. THE WELL WORK CREWS SKIPPED THIS STEP. THE FAILURE OF THE ISOLATING BARRIER INSTALLED AT 2,424 FEET MD IS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR.    THE ESTIMATED RELEASE VOLUME WAS CALCULATED USING THE WELL'S INFLOW PERFORMANCE RELATIONSHIP, THE RESERVOIR PRESSURE, AND THE PRESSURE IDENTIFIED AT SURFACE DURING THE RELEASE. AN ALTERNATIVE METHOD RESULTS IN A LOWER RELEASE VOLUME.

NARRATIVE: ON WEDNESDAY, JULY 10, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 21:04 HOURS, PG&E INCIDENT ON-DUTY PERSONNEL CONFIRMED A RELEASE OF GAS AT KETTLEMAN COMPRESSOR STATION RESULTED IN AN INJURY NECESSITATING IN-PATIENT HOSPITALIZATION.     FOLLOWING COMPLETION OF CONSTRUCTION, CLEARANCE ACTIVITIES TO RE-INTRODUCE GAS AND PURGE AIR FROM THE SYSTEM, INITIATED:   - THE APPROVED CLEARANCE REQUIRED V-56 TO BE "CHECKED OPEN" FOR PURGING, HOWEVER, IT HAD BEEN CLOSED FOR STEM SEAL REPLACEMENT WORK ON JULY 8, 2024, AND ONLY PARTIALLY OPENED PRIOR TO THE PURGE - OPERATIONS THAT HAD NOT BEEN DOCUMENTED NOR APPROVED AS PART OF THE SEQUENCE OF OPERATIONS IN THE CLEARANCE.   - GAS WAS RE-INTRODUCED TO THE SYSTEM FROM A 34'' CONTROL VALVE (V-90), A CLEARANCE POINT WITH 618 PSI. THERE ARE TWO WAYS TO OPERATE V-90, MANUAL HYDRAULIC AND MANUAL PNEUMATIC.   - WHEN ATTEMPTING TO MANUALLY OPERATE V-90 HYDRAULICALLY, OIL UNEXPECTEDLY DISCHARGED FROM THE ACTUATOR'S MANUAL HYDRAULIC OVERRIDE SYSTEM RELIEF VALVE AND THE VALVE FAILED TO OPERATE.   - V-90 WAS THEN PARTIALLY OPENED USING THE MANUAL PNEUMATIC CONTROLS. THIS METHOD IS NOT EFFECTIVE FOR FINE THROTTLING AS REQUIRED FOR PURGING IN DESIGN STANDARD A-38.    GAS FROM V-90 BEGAN TO DISPLACE AIR AT MULTIPLE VENT LOCATIONS PER THE ESTABLISHED CLEARANCE PLAN. IT IS SUSPECTED THAT AS A RESULT OF THE PARTIAL OPEN POSITION OF V-56, A GREATER AMOUNT OF GAS FLOW WAS DIRECTED TOWARD V-78. INSTEAD OF GAS EXITING THE 1/2'' VERTICAL VENT VALVE DOWNSTREAM OF V-78 AS APPROVED IN THE CLEARANCE, GAS EXITED THE FULL 6'' PIPE OPENING HORIZONTALLY WHERE THE BLIND FLANGE HAD BEEN REMOVED ON JULY 9. GAS FLOWED DIRECTLY INTO AN OPPOSING BLIND FLANGE ROUGHLY 20'' AWAY AT V-79. THIS RESULTED IN DEFLECTION IN ALL DIRECTIONS, INCLUDING INTO THE EXCAVATION BELOW. A HAZARDOUS AIR-GAS PLUME DEVELOPED. AT APPROXIMATELY 18:42 HOURS, THE AIR-GAS PLUME IGNITED, RESULTING IN SERIOUS BURNS TO ONE COWORKER AND MINOR INJURIES TO OTHERS. CWS IN THE AREA IMMEDIATELY RESPONDED, ATTENDING TO THE INJURED CW AND EXTINGUISHING VARIOUS SPOT FIRES USING PRE-STAGED FIRE EXTINGUISHERS. A CW CLOSED V-90 TO SHUT IN THE GAS BEFORE IGNITION, ALLOWING THE FLAME TO EXTINGUISH IN ABOUT ONE MINUTE.     PROCEDURE USE & ADHERENCE WAS THE APPARENT CAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT. CONFIGURATION CONTROL WAS NOT APPLIED WHEN CLEARANCE WORK WAS EXECUTED. PRIOR TO PURGING INTO SERVICE, CWS FAILED TO RECOGNIZE A HIGH ENERGY ESSENTIAL CONTROL HAD BEEN DISABLED DURING THE PURGE OUT OF SERVICE. PROCEDURES INVOLVING PURGING GAS FACILITIES, INSTALLATION AND OPERATION OF AIR MOVERS, AND TEMPORARY VENT STACKS PROVIDE A BARRIER IN THE FORM OF REQUIREMENTS TO CALCULATE AND MONITOR PURGE DRIVE PRESSURE, PROPERLY SIZE AIR MOVERS AND FRESH AIR SOURCES, AND INSTALL TEMPORARY VENT STACKS TO SAFELY DISPERSE GAS TO ATMOSPHERE. PROCEDURE INVOLVING NEW CLEARANCES FOR GT FACILITIES PROVIDES A BARRIER IN THE FORM OF CHANGE MANAGEMENT FOR THE CLEARANCE PROCESS AND ENDORSEMENT REQUIREMENTS, WHICH FAILED AS THE CLEARANCE TEAM DID NOT FOLLOW THEM.     THE PRECISE IGNITION SOURCE AND LOCATION COULD NOT BE DETERMINED TO A CERTAINTY; HOWEVER, THE FOLLOWING POTENTIAL IGNITION SOURCES WERE ASSESSED AND COULD NOT BE RULED OUT. AN ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE FROM THE GENERATED DUST CLOUD. AN ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE FROM EITHER THE PIPELINE ITSELF (DUE TO CHARGING FROM THE VENTING GAS) OR AN ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE FROM AN EMPLOYEE IN THE VICINITY OF THE VENTING GAS (DUE TO ELECTROSTATIC ACCUMULATION ON THEIR PERSON). A MECHANICAL SPARK FROM DEBRIS EXITING THE PIPELINE AT HIGH VELOCITY OR KICKED UP BY THE VENTING GAS. ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT IN THE VICINITY OF THE VENTING GAS WAS LOCKED OUT AND TAGGED OUT AND WAS RULED OUT AS A POTENTIAL IGNITION SOURCE.    THE INJURED EMPLOYEE WAS TRANSFERRED BY AMBULANCE TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL AND THEN MEDEVACKED TO A FRESNO AREA HOSPITAL TO RECEIVE CARE. THIS INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE DOT AND CPUC DUE TO A RELEASE OF GAS RESULTING IN AN INJURY REQUIRING HOSPITAL ADMISSION FOR OVERNIGHT STAY.

NAME: UGI UTILITIES, INC

UGI WAS ABLE TO STOP THE LEAK UNTIL THE FINAL REPAIR COULD BE MADE. BASED ON THE SMALL OPENING OF THE BODY BLEED VALVE, THE ESCAPING GAS WAS NEGLIGIBLE.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON MAY 20, 2024, AN INCIDENT OCCURRED ON PIPELINE SR- 538 IN BENTON, OHIO, DURING A SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE PROJECT. AS PART OF THE PROJECT, FOUR (4) TC ENERGY TECHNICIANS AND TWO (2) THIRD PARTY CONTRACTORS WERE WORKING TO INSTALL A SKILLET BLIND FLANGE TO ISOLATE THE AFFECTED PIPELINE SEGMENT. THE CREW OBSERVED A GAS LEAK FROM A 6-INCH VALVE AT THAT TIME AND DECIDED TO GREASE THE VALVE TO REMEDIATE THE LEAK USING A MOTORIZED GREASE GUN. AN IGNITION/FLASH FIRE ENSUED THAT INJURED TWO (2) OF THE TC ENERGY TECHNICIANS AND BOTH OF THE THIRD-PARTY CONTRACTORS. THE INJURED WORKERS WERE IMMEDIATELY TAKEN FOR MEDICAL EVALUATION AND TREATMENT. TC ENERGY COMPLETED AN INVESTIGATION TO IDENTIFY THE FACTORS THAT MAY HAVE CAUSED OR CONTRIBUTED TO THE INCIDENT. THE RESULTS OF THAT INVESTIGATION IDENTIFIED THE FOLLOWING PROPOSED RECOMMENDATIONS:   1. DEVELOP AND PUBLISH AN OPERATING PROCEDURE, OR UPDATE EXISTING PROCEDURES, TO OUTLINE THE REQUIREMENTS FOR INSTALLING A SKILLET BLIND.    2. CONDUCT A CONTROL OF WORK ASSESSMENT FOR INSTALLING SKILLET BLINDS TO PRODUCE A HAZARD CONTROLS DIAGRAM FOR REVIEW BY PERSONNEL WITH THE JOB SAFETY ANALYSIS (JSA).    3. IMPLEMENT IMPROVEMENTS TO PERSONNEL TRAINING MATERIALS TO PROVIDE MORE EMPHASIS ON THE ADEQUATE RESPONSE TO UNEXPECTED LEAKS.    4. CONDUCT RISK ASSESSMENT ON THE USAGE OF CSN SOLUTIONS BLACK WIDOW 20V GREASE GUNS.    5. UPDATE THE JSA FORM TO HAVE OPERATOR CONFIRM THE SPECIFIC PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) NEEDED FOR THE TASK (E.G., FLAME-RESISTANT CLOTHING, ETC.)    6. UPDATE APPLICABLE PROCEDURES TO REQUIRE A HOT WORK PERMIT TO BE COMPLETED WHEN INSTALLING A SKILLET BLIND DOWNSTREAM OF A SINGLE POINT OF ISOLATION REGARDLESS OF WHETHER A GAS LEAK OCCURS.    7. COMPLETE ONGOING EFFORT TO ISSUE PERSONAL DIFFUSIVE 4-GAS MONITOR GAS MONITORS TO ALL TC ENERGY FIELD TECHNICIANS AND OPERATIONS SPECIALISTS.   8. UPDATE JSA FORM TO CLARIFY THAT CONTRACTORS MUST ALSO SIGN THE JSA IF THEY ARE ALSO INVOLVED IN THE TASK BEING COVERED.   9. SHARE ADDITIONAL DETAILS AND LEARNINGS FROM THE INCIDENT TO THE ORGANIZATION.   10. UPDATE GAS HANDLING PROCEDURES TO CLARIFY THE AMOUNT OF TIME SINCE THE LAST VALVE INSPECTION / SERVICING THAT WOULD TRIGGER ADDITIONAL INSPECTION / SERVICING BEFORE COMPLETING A LOCKOUT TAG OUT ACTIVITY.      TC ENERGY SENT THE VALVE ASSOCIATED WITH THE INCIDENT TO A LABORATORY FOR FURTHER ANALYSIS.  THE LAB RESULT CONFIRMED THE SOURCE OF THE GAS LEAK WAS THE VALVE. THE FOLLOWING ARE THE RESULT OF TESTS;  1-THE SEAT TESTS CONDUCTED IN GENERAL ACCORDANCE WITH THE 24TH EDITION OF API 6D, SPECIFICATION FOR PIPELINE AND PIPING VALVES, SHOWED THAT THERE WAS A DETECTABLE LEAK AT THE VALVE SEAT OF THE SUBJECT PLUG VALVE AT PRESSURES AS LOW AS 70 PSI.   2-THE SHELL TESTS CONDUCTED IN GENERAL ACCORDANCE WITH THE 24TH EDITION OF API 6D SHOWED THAT THERE WAS A DETECTABLE LEAK AT THE FLANGED CONNECTION BETWEEN THE ROTATING SHAFT OF THE PLUG AND THE SHELL OF THE VALVE AT PRESSURES AS LOW AS 800 PSI.

NARRATIVE: AN ACCIDENTAL IGNITION OCCURRED AT STATION 60 ON MAY 8, 2024, AN INTERSTATE TRANSMISSION COMPRESSOR STATION OPERATED BY TRANSCONTINENTAL PIPE LINE COMPANY, LLC (TRANSCO) NEAR JACKSON, LOUISIANA. AT THE TIME, STATION 60 WAS OFFLINE AND ISOLATED FROM OPERATING PIPELINES FOR SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE TO REPLACE INTERNAL VALVE COMPONENTS CONNECTING THE COMPRESSOR UNITS TO THE STATION'S COMMON SUCTION AND DISCHARGE HEADERS. THE INCIDENT HAPPENED AT 6:32 AM, JUST BEFORE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE WORK WAS TO BEGIN FOR THAT DAY.   THE FACILITY'S CONSTRUCTION PROVIDED FOR SINGLE VALVE ISOLATION BETWEEN EACH PIPELINE AND FACILITY PIPING. WORK PLANS ANTICIPATED LEAKAGE AT THESE ISOLATION POINTS AND INCORPORATED AN AIR PURGE PLAN TO MITIGATE POTENTIAL FLAMMABLE ENVIRONMENTS WITHIN PIPING.     THE ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE FOLLOWING CAUSES DIRECTLY LED TO THE CONSEQUENCES OF THIS INCIDENT:     1. FLAMMABLE MATERIAL (NATURAL GAS) LEAKED INTO THE STATION PIPING AROUND THE PROCESS ISOLATION BETWEEN THE STATION AND TRANSMISSION PIPELINES;  2. THE MITIGATIVE AIR FLOW DID NOT MAINTAIN FLAMMABLE GAS CONCENTRATION BELOW THE LEL;  3. THE MITIGATIVE AIR FLOW DRIED INTERNAL SLUDGE DEPOSITS INSIDE THE STATION PIPING;  4. SUSPECTED ACCUMULATION OF PYROPHORIC IRON SULFIDE IN THE INTERNAL SLUDGE DEPOSITS OF THE STATION PIPING IGNITED UPON EXPOSURE TO OXYGEN; AND  5. A PERSON WAS PRESENT WITHIN THE FIRE ZONE AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENTAL IGNITION. THIS INCLUDES PROVIDING COMPREHENSIVE GUIDANCE AND CONDUCTING REFRESHER TRAINING FOR ALL PERSONNEL INVOLVED. BY REINFORCING THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NECESSARY FOR SAFE OPERATIONS, WILLIAMS AIMS TO ENSURE THAT PERSONNEL ARE EQUIPPED TO RECOGNIZE POTENTIAL HAZARDS AND RESPOND APPROPRIATELY. NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON 4/16/2024, OPERATIONS WERE PERFORMING VALVE MAINTENANCE ON PL-115 GATE VALVE (WKM VALVE WITH AN EIM ACTUATOR). DURING THE CLOSE ACTUATION, THE VALVE FAILED TO STOP CLOSING WHEN COMMANDED AND RESULTED IN THE ACTUATOR BEING PUSH OFF THE STEM AND INTO THE GROUND.     THE END OF STROKE/LIMIT VALVE FAILED TO ISOLATE POWER GAS AFTER CLOSE, RESULTING IN ADDITIONAL TORQUE ENERGY BEING APPLIED TO THE GEARS HOUSING. ALL THAT ENERGY RESULTED IN THE FAILURE OF THE CAST IRON WELDS BETWEEN THE ACTUATOR AND YOKE/STEM HOUSING. WITH THE GEAR HOUSING OFF THE SHAFT, THE GATE VALVE COULD NOT REMAIN CLOSED AND PIPELINE PRESSURE SLAMMED IT OPEN AGAINST THE BONNET.     AS A RESULT OF THE ACTUATOR FAILURE, A STAINLESS POWER GAS LINE BROKE OFF AND VENTED.    THE EIM ACTUATOR CONTROLS WERE TESTED ON A BENCH WITH PRESSURIZED AIR AND DISCOVERED TO SUCCESSFULLY ACHIEVE THE OPEN LIMIT BUT NOT THE CLOSE LIMIT. THE CAUSE FOR THIS WAS THE CLOSE LIMIT VALVE WAS INSTALLED BACKWARDS, WHICH RESULTED IN THE POPPET BEING UNABLE TO ENGAGE WITH THE CAM AND FAILURE TO ISOLATE POWER GAS TO THE MOTOR ONCE THE VALVE WAS CLOSED.

NARRATIVE: THE INCIDENT TOOK PLACE AT FARMER BROTHERS METERING AND REGULATING STATION BEGINNING AT 20:41 ON MARCH 25, 2024. WHEN THE SUMP LEVEL EXCEEDS A CERTAIN THRESHOLD, THE CONTROLLER ACTUATES THE CONTROL VALVE TO THE OPEN POSITION TO RELEASE LIQUIDS TO A WASTE TANK. THE CONTROL VALVE'S MECHANICAL LEVEL CONTROLLER FAILED TO REVERT POSITION ONCE THE LIQUID LEVEL IN THE SUMP HAD DROPPED BELOW THE DESIGN THRESHOLD. GAS FLOWED FROM THE SEPARATOR THROUGH A 2" NPS PIPE INTO A WASTE TANK AND THEN ENTERED THE ATMOSPHERE THROUGH THE TANK BLOWOFF VALVES UNTIL THE AFTERNOON OF MARCH 26, 2024 AT 14:45 WHEN THE INCIDENT WAS DISCOVERED.    UPON ARRIVAL AT THE FACILITY, PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY SHUT THE MANUAL VALVE TO THE LIQUIDS TANK WHICH CEASED EMISSIONS OF NATURAL GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE AT 15:07 ON MARCH 26, 2024. THE CONTROLLER ON THE CONTROL VALVE WAS FOUND TO BE MISALIGNED BECAUSE THE SPRING TENSION WAS TOO HIGH, NOT ALLOWING THE VALVE TO CLOSE. THE VALVE'S CONTROLLER WAS IMMEDIATELY RECALIBRATED, RESET, AND TESTED TO ENSURE FUNCTIONALITY.

NARRATIVE: ON 2/29/24, NATURAL GAS COMPRESSOR UNIT B (UNIT B) WAS STOPPED DURING ROUTINE SHUTDOWN; THIS ACTION ISSUES A "CLOSE" COMMAND TO UNIT B'S REMOTE ACTUATED SUCTION VALVE SD2401B. SDV2401B'S ACTUATOR USES A SOLENOID VALVE (VERSA VALVE) WHICH IS RESPONSIBLE FOR SDV2401B'S ACTUATOR OPERATION. THE SOLENOID VALVE MALFUNCTIONED PARTWAY THROUGH THE CLOSURE OF SDV2401B. SHORTLY AFTER, THE SCADA SYSTEM ALERTED THE CONTROLLER THAT SDV2401B FAILED TO CLOSE. THE ALERT WAS ACCOMPANIED BY ADDITIONAL ALARMS, 38 ALARMS IN A 40 SECOND PERIOD, WHICH INCLUDED NUISANCE ALARMS RELATED TO THE COMPRESSOR SHUTDOWN AS WELL AS ALARMS FROM UNRELATED FACILITY ACTIVITIES. ALL ALARMS WERE ACKNOWLEDGED BY THE CONTROLLER. SDV2401B REMAINED IN ALARM STATE AND SDV2401B WAS LEFT PARTIALLY OPEN.    A SHORT TIME LATER, THE CONTROLLER ISSUED A SCADA COMMAND TO STOP THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING FAN SYSTEM, WHICH, BY DESIGN, AUTOMATICALLY TRIGGERS A BLOW-DOWN OF ALL GAS PIPING INSIDE THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING VIA THE FACILITY BLOW-DOWN SYSTEM BY ISSUING AN 'OPEN' COMMAND TO BYPASS VALVE XXV2404B AND BLOW-DOWN VALVE BDV2411B. THIS BLOW-DOWN PROCESS IS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE BUILDING SAFE TO WORK IN.    WITH SDV2401B STILL IN A PARTIALLY OPEN POSITION AND XXV2404B AND BDV2411B IN THE OPEN POSITION, A FLOW PATH WAS PRESENT FOR GAS TO CONTINUOUSLY FLOW FROM THE SUCTION SIDE OF THE COMPRESSOR UNIT B TO THE FACILITY BLOW-DOWN SYSTEM, RESULTING IN A CONTINUOUS RELEASE OF GAS @ 600 MSCF/H. ON 3/1/2024, THE MEASUREMENT TECH RECOGNIZED AN ISSUE WITH A GAS FLOW TOTALIZER IMBALANCE AND THEN DISCUSSED THE ISSUE WITH THE ON-SHIFT CONTROLLER. THE OPERATIONS TEAM INSPECTED THE FACILITY BLOW-DOWN SYSTEM AND IDENTIFIED GAS VENTING FROM THE TOP OF THE BLOW-DOWN SILENCER. IMMEDIATE ACTION WAS TAKEN TO CLOSE THE FACILITY'S BLOW-DOWN SYSTEM AND HALT THE GAS RELEASE.     SDV2401B WAS STROKED TO TROUBLESHOOT AND TEST WHAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN NORMAL FUNCTION. THE ACTUATOR SOLENOID VALVE (VERSA VALVE) WAS SERVICED, AND PROPER OPENING/CLOSURE WAS VERIFIED WITH SDV2401B.

NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEJAS PIPELINE
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: KINDER MORGAN TEJAS GAS CONTROL RECEIVED A CALL FROM A HOMEOWNER OF A POTENTIAL NATURAL GAS LEAK.  KM OPERATIONS PERSONNEL RESPONDED AND VERIFIED THE PRESENCE OF GAS ABOVEGROUND ON ITS 202-600 LINE.  NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER AND THE TXRRC.  OPERATIONS WERE DISPATCHED TO THE UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES AND LOCAL EMERGENCY RESPONDERS (HOUSTON FIRE DEPARTMENT) WERE CONTACTED AND DISPATCHED.  UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES WERE CLOSED IN ORDER THAT THE PIPELINE SEGMENT COULD BE ISOLATED, AND THE PIPELINE BLOWN DOWN.  THE LEAK SITE WAS EXCAVATED, AND EVALUATION AND REPAIR OF THE LEAK BEGAN.  DURING EVALUATION THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE FROM A CRACK AT A TAP WELD (TAP HAD PREVIOUSLY BEEN ABANDONED). THE REPAIR OF THE LEAK CONSISTED OF THE SEGMENT OF PIPE CONTAINING THE ABANDONED TAP BEING CUT OUT AND REPLACED WITH A PIECE OF STRAIGHT PIPE.  THE KINDER MORGAN METALLURGY DEPARTMENT IS CURRENTLY IN THE PROCESS OF COMPLETING A FAILURE ANALYSIS OF THE FAILED TAP CONNECTION.  UPON THE COMPLETION OF THE FAILURE ANALYSIS INVESTIGATION THIS REPORT WILL BE UPDATED AND FINALIZED.      ON MAY 9, 2024; KINDER MORGAN'S METALLURGICAL ENGINEER COMPLETED THE FAILURE ANALYSIS OF THE TAP CONNECTION.  THE FINAL CONCLUSIONS AS TO THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE WERE: 1) THE LEAK WAS LOCATED AT THE TOE OF THE FILLET WELD ATTACHING A LOCALIZED SADDLE TO THE NPS 20 PIPE; 2) THE HOT TAP CONNECTION DID NOT HAVE A FULL ENCIRCLEMENT SADDLE, AND 3) THE FRACTURE WAS A DUCTILE OVERLOAD CAUSED BY A DOWNWARD BENDING MOMENT ON THE NPS 2 BRANCH.    PLEASE NOTE THAT CURRENT KINDER MORGAN ENGINEERING STANDARD E1100 WOULD NOT PERMIT NEW CONSTRUCTION WITH THIS NPS 2 ON NPS 20 HOT TAP CONFIGURATION WITH ONLY A LOCALIZED SADDLE AND NO FULL ENCIRCLEMENT SLEEVE.

NAME: EASTERN GAS TRANSMISSION AND STORAGE, INC.
NARRATIVE: OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT RECEIVED INITIAL NOTIFICATION OF THIS INCIDENT VIA A CALL FROM ANOTHER OPERATOR ON 1/25/24 AT APPROXIMATELY 18:06 REPORTING THAT THERE WAS A FIRE AT BIG ISAAC COMPRESSOR STATION (CS) (GA-1081). GAS CONTROL RECEIVED SECONDARY NOTIFICATION OF THIS INCIDENT FROM 911 AT APPROXIMATELY 18:10 REPORTING THAT A FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS IN THE PROCESS OF RESPONDING TO BIG ISAAC CS. AT THIS POINT IN TIME, THE EXTENT AND SEVERITY OF THE FIRE AT BIG ISAAC CS WAS NOT KNOWN. BIG ISAAC CS RECEIVES NATURAL GAS FROM H-21912 (PRODUCTION PIPELINE OWNED AND OPERATED BY HOPE GAS), COMPRESSES IT USING A SINGLE ENGINE UNIT (AJAX MODEL #DPC-360LE INSTALLED IN 1999 WITH 360 HP), AND DISCHARGES IT INTO TL-413 (GATHERING PIPELINE OWNED AND OPERATED BY EGTS WITH A MAOP OF 500 PSIG). GAS CONTROL NOTIFIED OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT OF THE SITUATION AT APPROXIMATELY 18:15. OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT DISPATCHED PERSONNEL TO BIG ISAAC CS AT APPROXIMATELY 18:20. GAS CONTROL LOST COMMUNICATIONS WITH BIG ISAAC CS AT APPROXIMATELY 17:19. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT BIG ISAAC CS AT APPROXIMATELY 19:24, ASSESSED THE SITUATION, BEGAN UTILIZING FIRE EXTINGUISHERS TO EXTINGUISH THE FIRE ON THE ENGINE UNIT, AND IMPLEMENTED A PLAN TO SAFELY ISOLATE THE FIRE. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL MANUALLY CLOSED VALVE 1081-A AT APPROXIMATELY 19:26. VALVE 1081-A IS LOCATED WHERE THE DISCHARGE OF BIG ISAAC CS CONNECTS TO TL-413 WHICH IS DOWNSTREAM OF THE FIRE. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL MANUALLY CLOSED VALVE 1081-B AT APPROXIMATELY 19:27. VALVE 1081-B IS LOCATED WHERE THE SUCTION OF BIG ISAAC CS CONNECTS TO H-21912 WHICH IS UPSTREAM OF THE FIRE. THE CLOSURE OF VALVES 1081-A AND 1081-B COMPLETED THE ISOLATION OF THE FIRE. THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED AT APPROXIMATELY 19:36. THE RESPONDING FIRE DEPARTMENT DEPARTED THE FACILITY AT APPROXIMATELY 20:20. THE RESPONDING OPERATIONS PERSONNEL SECURED THE FACILITY AND DEPARTED THE FACILITY AT APPROXIMATELY 23:20. NO EVACUATIONS WERE NECESSARY, NO INJURIES WERE SUSTAINED, AND THERE WERE NO ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AS A RESULT OF THE INCIDENT. BASED ON REVIEW OF THE SCADA DISCHARGE PRESSURE AND FLOW HISTORIES, IT IS BELIEVED THAT THE FIRE ON THE ENGINE UNIT INITIALLY IGNITED AT APPROXIMATELY 17:19 AT WHICH POINT IN TIME BIG ISAAC CS WAS IN NORMAL OPERATION WITH A DISCHARGE PRESSURE OF 197 PSIG AND A DISCHARGE FLOW RATE OF 832 MSCFD. UPON EXAMINATION OF THE ENGINE UNIT FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT, IT IS BELIEVED THAT THE FIRE INITIATED IN THE LOW STAGE DISTANCE PIECE AND WAS SUSTAINED BY THE FLOW OF NATURAL GAS. THE CROSSHEAD PIN AND BUSHING SEIZED CAUSING INCREASED FRICTION ON THE SLIDE ASSEMBLY. THE ADDITIONAL FRICTION INCREASED THE TEMPERATURE ON THE COMPONENTS TO THE FLASHPOINT OF THE OIL (459 DEG F). THE CROSSHEAD RUNNING POSITION WAS ALTERED BY MELTING BABBITT CAUSING THE COMPRESSOR PISTON ROD TO RUB THE PRESSURE AND WIPER PACKING CASES. EXCESSIVE RUBBING OF THE COMPRESSOR PISTON ROD GENERATED EXCESSIVE HEAT INSIDE A GASEOUS ENVIRONMENT WHICH ALLOWED COMBUSTION TO OCCUR. THE INTERNAL FIRE MELTED THE PLEXIGLASS COVER ON THE CROSSHEAD DISTANCE PIECE HOUSING WHICH ALLOWED ADDITIONAL OXYGEN TO ENTER THE DISTANCE PIECE AND SUSTAINED THE COMBUSTION. THE RESULTING DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE UNIT AND THE ASSOCIATED FRAME, SKID, PROTECTIVE STRUCTURE, CONTROL PANEL, COMPRESSOR BOTTLE, FUEL LINE VALVE, AND CONDUIT WAS EXTENSIVE. INITIAL TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ON 1/25/24 AT 19:28. THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ASSIGNED INCIDENT REPORT #1389962 TO THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION OF THE INCIDENT. A FOLLOW UP TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ON 1/27/24 AT 09:04 TO CONFIRM THE INITIAL TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION. THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ASSIGNED INCIDENT REPORT #1389962 TO THE FOLLOW UP TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION. THE DECISION WAS MADE TO ABANDON BIG ISAAC CS AS AN ENGINE UNIT AT LAW CS IS CAPABLE OF MOVING THE NATURAL GAS THAT WAS MOVED BY THE ENGINE UNIT AT BIG ISAAC CS.

NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 17, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 06:20 HRS. CST, TC ENERGY WAS NOTIFIED BY THE PUBLIC OF A POTENTIAL GAS RELEASE AT THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION, LOCATED IN ALCORN COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI, AND DISCOVERED NATURAL GAS BEING RELEASED TO ATMOSPHERE. THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE WAS CONFIRMED BY TC ENERGY OPERATIONS AT APPROXIMATELY 07:16 HRS. CST. IT WAS LATER CONFIRMED THAT THE BLOWDOWN VALVE'S (5SH-2D BD) STRATIX SWITCH, WHICH COMMUNICATES THE VALVE STATUS TO THE PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC), HAD MALFUNCTIONED. THIS LOSS OF COMMUNICATION CAUSED THE BLOWDOWN VALVE TO LOSE ITS HOLD CLOSED COMMAND FROM THE PLC. THE VALVE TRAVELED OPEN DUE TO THE LOSS OF SIGNAL WHEN THE SWITCH FAILED. THE MALFUNCTIONING SWITCH ALSO CAUSED NO ALARM TO BE CONVEYED TO THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN DEVICE (ESD) PLC AND THEREFORE, IS THE REASON GAS CONTROLLER DID NOT RECEIVE A "CALL OUT" ALARM FROM THE SCADA SYSTEM. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS MANUALLY CLOSED THE BLOWDOWN VALVE AT 08:05 HRS. CST. THE STRATIX SWITCH WAS REPLACED AND THE ESD SYSTEM WAS PLACED BACK INTO NORMAL SERVICE AT APPROXIMATELY 12:30 HRS. CST. THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION WAS NOT SHUT DOWN DUE TO THIS INCIDENT.

NAME: GREAT LAKES GAS TRANSMISSION LIMITED PARTNERSHIP
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 12, 2024, SEVERE WEATHER INCLUDING HEAVY WINDS AND SNOW PASSED THROUGH THE GAYLORD, MICHIGAN AREA. WHEN THE POWER FAILURE ALARM WAS DETECTED AT 7:23 PM. EST, THE MONITORING CENTER CALLED THE TECHNICIAN ON SITE TO INVESTIGATE THE ALARM. THE TECHNICIAN COULD AUDIBLY HEAR BLOWING GAS AT 7:47 P.M. INITIAL EXCAVATION BEGAN ON JANUARY 2, 2024. FIVE FEET OF THE M730A LINE WAS EXPOSED WHERE THE LEAK WAS THOUGHT TO HAVE ORIGINATED. AFTER INVESTIGATING THE EXPOSED AREA, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE LEAK WAS NOT IN THIS AREA. FIELD OPERATIONS BEGAN PROBING THE AREA WEST AND EAST OF THE EXPOSED PORTION OF THE LINE TO INVESTIGATE FURTHER. BOTH AREAS THAT WERE PROBED AND BAR-HOLE TESTED WITH THE 46 HAWK LEAK DETECTOR. FIELD OPERATIONS WORKED WITH FACILITY PLANNING TO DEVELOP A PLAN TO LOWER THE OPERATION PRESSURE OF THE M730A TO AS LOW AS 50 PSIG IN ORDER TO SLOW THE LEAK AS WELL AS KEEP FARM TAP CUSTOMERS IN SERVICE. BACKFILL AND TOPSOIL RESTORATION WAS COMPLETED ON JANUARY 23, 2024. THE COMPANY DID NOT CONFIRM THAT THE STORAGE FIELD WAS LIKELY THE SOURCE OF THE GAS UNTIL JANUARY 30, 2024, THE DATE AN INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER (NRC) IN ACCORDANCE WITH PHMSA REPORTING CRITERIA.      ON NOVEMBER 26, 2023, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL BEGAN AN EARLY WITHDRAWAL FROM THE UNDERGROUND STORAGE FIELD TO REDUCE THE PRESSURE IN THE FIELD, A DAY EARLIER THAN WITHDRAWAL HAD PREVIOUSLY BEEN PLANNED. ON JANUARY 30TH, 2024, A GAS SAMPLE ANALYSIS REPORT CONFIRMED THAT THE GAS DISCOVERED IN THE LANDOWNER'S WATER WELL LIKELY ORIGINATED FROM THE STORAGE FIELD. AT THAT TIME, SALTVILLE GAS DEEMED THE EVENT SIGNIFICANT WITHIN THE MEANING OF THE PHMSA "INCIDENT" DEFINITION (SEE 49 CFR 191.3(3)) EVEN THOUGH IT DID NOT MEET THE OTHER INCIDENT CRITERIA UNDER 49 CFR 191.3(1) OR (2). THEREFORE, ON JANUARY 30TH, 2024, AT 9:59 A.M. ET, SALTVILLE STORAGE NOTIFIED NRC.    SUPPLEMENTAL 07/16/2025  ON APRIL 22, 2024, SALTVILLE GAS CONDUCTED NITROGEN PRESSURE TESTS ON STORAGE WELLS EH-87, EH-90 AND EH-93. BOTH WELLS EH-87 AND EH-90 WERE ABLE TO MAINTAIN PRESSURE FOR THE DURATION OF THE TESTING PERIOD, INDICATING EACH WELLS' PRODUCTION CASING WAS INTACT. THE AFFECTED CASING WAS REMOVED AND SENT TO A THIRD-PARTY LABORATORY FOR ANALYSIS. THIRD-PARTY METALLURGICAL TEST RESULTS CONFIRMED THAT THE THROUGH-WALL DEFECT WAS PRIMARILY CAUSED BY MICROBIOLOGICALLY INFLUENCED EXTERNAL CORROSION.

NAME: CONSUMERS ENERGY CO
NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 8, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 12:11 HOURS CONSUMERS ENERGY GAS CONTROL RECEIVED AN ALARM NOTIFICATION WHICH INDICATED A POSSIBLE FIRE AT THE ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION (PLANT 4 DEHYDRATION SYSTEM BUILDING). THE CONSUMERS ENERGY ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION IS IN IRA, MICHIGAN (ST. CLAIR COUNTY).    A STATION MECHANIC AT THE SITE WAS NOTIFIED AND CONFIRMED ACTIVATION OF THE PLANT FIRE-GATE SYSTEM OCCURRED DUE TO THE FIRE DETECTION ALARM. FOLLOWING THE EVENT, THE PLANT WAS REMOVED FROM SERVICE AND THE SCENE WAS MADE SAFE. ADDITIONAL PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED TO THE STATION TO DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL CAUSE OF THE ACTIVATION.     DURING THE INCIDENT INVESTIGATION, NO NOTABLE INDICATIONS OF FAILURES WERE PRESENT IN THE FACILITY, BUT UPON ARRIVAL, IT WAS NOTED THAT A GAP IN THE INSULATION ON THE REBOILER EXHAUST STACK WAS CLEARLY VISIBLE AND WAS PRESUMED TO BE THE SOURCE OF A FALSE TRIP INDICATION TO THE FIRE-EYE (IN DIRECT LINE OF SIGHT) DUE TO THE INFRARED IRRADIATION FROM THE PIPE (OPERATING AS NORMAL UP TO 1500 DEGREE F). THE INSULATION ON THE EXHAUST SYSTEM WAS INSPECTED WITH NO NOTABLE ISSUES OBSERVED, REPAIRED, AND RETURNED TO SERVICE ON NOVEMBER 9, 2023.    ON NOVEMBER 10, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 11:17 HOURS, LESS THAN 24 HOURS AFTER THE RETURN TO SERVICE CONSUMERS ENERGY GAS CONTROL RECEIVED AN ALARM NOTIFICATION WHICH INDICATED A POSSIBLE FIRE AT THE ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION (PLANT 4 DEHYDRATION SYSTEM BUILDING). THE EQUIPMENT WAS TAKEN OFF-LINE, AND ALL INSULATION WAS REMOVED TO PERMIT PHYSICAL INSPECTION. SEVERAL CRACKED WELDS WERE IDENTIFIED ON THE EXHAUST LINE OF THE THERMAL OXIDIZER, SUPER HEATER, AND CONDENSATE COLLECTION SYSTEM OF THE THERMAL OXIDIZER. LOOSE BOLTS WERE FOUND IN THE FLANGED CONNECTIONS OF THE SYSTEM, AND AN EXHAUST PIPE SLIP JOINT CONNECTION TO THE EXHAUST STACK WAS FOUND TO NO LONGER BE INSERTED INTO THE FITTING.    BOTH EVENTS WERE REPORTED TO MPSC AS REQUIRED WHEN AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SYSTEM IS ACTIVATED, AND GAS RELEASED. HOWEVER, A MORE IN-DEPTH VISUAL INSPECTION CONFIRMED ADDITIONAL EQUIPMENT DAMAGE ANTICIPATED TO EXCEED PHMSA REPORTING CRITERIA OF $139,700.     ADDITIONAL INVESTIGATIONS AFTER THE EVENT HAVE IDENTIFIED A CONCERN RELATIVE TO INSUFFICIENT BOLT TORQUE SPECIFICATIONS USED DURING A 2020 REPAIR TO THE SYSTEM, PIPE FABRICATION FAILURE RESULTING IN PRE-STRESS BEING APPLIED TO THE FAILED SYSTEM CONNECTION POINTS, AND POTENTIAL PINNED PIPE IN A HIGH THERMAL GROWTH AREA OF THE SYSTEM EXACERBATING STRESSES IMPARTED TO THOSE SAME CONNECTION POINTS. FURTHER PROBLEM SOLVING IS REQUIRED TO DETERMINE THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE. HOWEVER, WITH THE CONCERNS DEFINED, CONSUMERS ENERGY HAS TAKEN ACTION TO REMEDIATE EACH CONCERN THROUGH A REFABRICATION OF THE SUPER HEATER VESSEL FAILED COMPONENTS, PIPE ASSEMBLIES FOUND TO BE CREATING THE PRE-STRESS SCENARIO, SLIP JOINT INSERTION WAS INCREASED TO AVOID RISK OF THE JOINT FAILING, APPLICATION OF TORQUE SPECIFICATIONS FROM THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE FOR RE-VALIDATING TORQUE ON BOLTED CONNECTIONS FOLLOWING RETURN TO SERVICE.    FURTHER ANALYSIS IS REQUIRED TO SUPPORT CONFIRMATION OF THE PIPE FAILURE MODES IDENTIFIED IN THE FIELD AND IS PRESENTLY UNDERWAY. THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER HAS BEEN ENGAGED IN THE REVIEW AND REPAIR PLAN AND IS SUPPORTING REVIEW OF THE STRESS ANALYSIS. ENGINEERING SUPPORT HAS BEEN CONTRACTED TO SUPPORT MODEL DEVELOPMENT OF THE SYSTEM AND EXECUTE A PIPE STRESS ANALYSIS. FOLLOWING THE OUTCOME OF THE MODELING AND VALIDATION OF THE FAILURE MODES, ADDITIONAL STEPS MAY BE NECESSARY TO IMPROVE THE INTEGRITY OF THE SYSTEM AND WILL BE IMPLEMENTED ACCORDINGLY.    FURTHER ANALYSIS CONFIRMED THE FAILURE WAS A RESULT OF INSUFFICIENT BOLT TORQUE SPECIFICATIONS PROVIDED BY THE MANUFACTURER DURING A PREVIOUS REPAIR TO THE SYSTEM. THE FAILURE WAS A RESULT OF THE BOLTS YIELDING AND TORQUE WAS LOST THROUGH THE THERMAL CYCLE CAUSING BOLTS TO LOOSEN.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON OCTOBER 5, 2023 AT 06:58 (EST), STATION 267 IN HOPKINTON, MA EXPERIENCED AN ESD EVENT. THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION WAS RECEIVED VIA SCADA ALARMS. GAS CONTROL PERSONNEL NOTIFIED TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WHO WERE IN ROUTE TO THE STATION FOR DAILY ACTIVITIES. TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED ONSITE AT 07:11 (EST). THE HOPKINTON FIRE DEPARTMENT HAD BEEN NOTIFIED BY A THIRD-PARTY AND ARRIVED ONSITE AT 07:18 (EST).  ONCE TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED ONSITE, THEY OBSERVED THAT STATION 267 WAS VENTING, BUT THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS NOT FULLY ISOLATED FROM THE MAINLINE. DURING A STATION WALKTHROUGH BY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE COMPRESSOR STATION SIDE GATE VALVES WERE PARTIALLY OPEN. THUS GAS FROM THE MAINLINE WAS VENTING THROUGH THE STATION. AT 7:38 (EST), TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL CLOSED THE COMPRESSOR STATION BLOWOFF VALVES TO STOP VENTING OF THE GAS. AT 3:00 (EST), STATION 267 WAS CONFIRMED TO BE ISOLATED FROM THE MAINLINE. SINCE THIS EVENT, STATION 267 HAS REMAINED ISOLATED.   FOLLOWING THE INTERNAL INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT A POWER FAULT IN THE AREA RESULTED IN THE FAILURE OF THE STATION PLC. THE PLC FAILURE ACTIVATED THE BUILDING PROTECTION SYSTEM, TRIGGERING THE ESD. DUE TO THE ESD COMMAND, THE COMPRESSOR STATION VENT VALVES WERE OPENED TO BLOW DOWN THE UNITS. HOWEVER, THE COMPRESSOR SIDE GATE VALVES FAILED TO PROPERLY CLOSE AND ISOLATE THE STATION. THE GAS LOSS DUE TO THIS EVENT WAS CALCULATED TO BE 8664 MCF.  IN ORDER TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, NEW PLCS HAVE BEEN ORDERED AND WILL BE INSTALLED. ADDITIONALLY, ALL OF THE COMPRESSOR STATION SIDE GATE VALVES HAVE BEEN EVALUATED TO ENSURE CORRECT FUNCTIONALITY.  AS AN ADDED PRECAUTION, OPERATIONS HAS DEVELOPED A PROCEDURE FOR ISOLATING THE STATION FROM THE MAINLINE DURING EXTENDED PERIODS WHEN THE STATION IS NOT IN DEMAND. NAME: MIDCONTINENT EXPRESS PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON 06/27/2023 AT 12:00 PM, MIDCONTINENT EXPRESS PIPELINE (MEP) HAD A REPORTABLE GAS RELEASE THAT OCCURRED AT THE MEP 2 COMPRESSOR STATION WHEN THE ESD SYSTEM WAS ACTIVATED AND THE DISCHARGE SIDE OF THE ESD SYSTEM DID NOT OPERATE AS DESIGNED. THE ESD WAS ACTIVATED AS A RESULT OF LOSS OF UPS POWER SUPPLY. THE USE OF THE UPS POWER WAS INITIATED BY A TRIPPED ELECTRICAL BREAKER THAT WAS CAUSED BY AN ELECTRICALLY SHORTED AIR COMPRESSOR.      THE ESD BLOCK VALVE THAT IS HELD CLOSED BY AN ENERGIZED SOLENOID, WHEN SUPPLIED BY COMMERCIAL OR UPS POWER. WHEN UPS BATTERIES WERE DRAINED, THE STATION LOST CONTROL POWER TO THE STATION COMPUTERS, PLCS AND UNIT HMIS. THE LOSS OF COMMERCIAL POWER DUE TO TRIPPED BREAKER AND THE LOSS OF UPS POWER ALLOWED THE ESD VALVE TO OPEN CAUSING THE STATION TO BLOWDOWN THROUGH A FULLY PNEUMATIC SYSTEM. THE ESD SYSTEM BY DESIGN  HAS AN INTERLOCK PROCESS SO THAT THE BLOWDOWN VALVES WILL NOT OPEN UNLESS THE ASSOCIATED STATION SIDE GATE VALVES CLOSE. THIS IS ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH A SERIES OF TRIGGER VALVES.  THE SUCTION SIDE OF THE STATION WORKED AS DESIGNED DURING THE ESD. THE INVESTIGATION FOUND EXCESSIVE CORROSION/RUST WITHIN THE INTERNAL WORKINGS OF THE TWO SHAFER VALVES. THE SHAFER TRIGGER VALVES WERE REPLACED, THE TRIPPED BREAKER WAS RESET, THE SHORTED AIR COMPRESSOR WAS REMOVED FROM SERVICE UNTIL THE MOTOR WAS REPLACED, THE DISCHARGE SIDE GATE AND EDS DISCHARGE BLOWDOWN VALVE WERE RETURN TO THEIR NORMAL STATE AND THE STATION WAS PLACED BACK ONLINE.

NAME: FRONTIER NATURAL GAS COMPANY
CAUSE_DETAILS: DAMAGE BY OPERATOR OR OPERATOR'S CONTRACTOR NOT RELATED TO EXCAVATION AND NOT DUE TO MOTORIZED VEHICLE/EQUIPMENT DAMAGE
NARRATIVE: WHEN THE AREA WAS EXCAVATED IN 2022 TO REPAIR THE LEAK, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE PIPING INSTALLED UNDER THE ROAD DID NOT ALIGN WITH ANOTHER SECTION OF PIPE AND A WRINKLE BEND EXISTED BETWEEN THE TWO SECTIONS. RATHER THAN REWORKING THE AREA SO THAT THE PIPES WOULD MORE CLOSELY ALIGN, FRONTIER BELIEVES THAT THE CONTRACTOR WHO INSTALLED THE PIPE IN 1999 USED EQUIPMENT TO MANIPULATE THE LOCATION OF THE PIPE THROUGH PULLING AND/OR PUSHING TO ALIGN THE PIPES SO THAT THEY COULD BE JOINED VIA WELDING. THE SECTION OF PIPE WITH THE WRINKLE BEND IS BELIEVED TO HAVE BEEN INSTALLED WITH A DIRECTIONAL DRILL AS IT IS UNDER A ROAD SO THE CONTRACTOR DID NOT WANT TO OPEN CUT THE ROAD TO CORRECT THE ISSUE. DURING THE PROCESS TO MANIPULATE THE PIPING, THE WRINKLE BEND WAS CREATED WHICH CRACKED THE COATING AND OVER TIME ALLOWED FOR CORROSION TO CREATE A HOLE INSIDE OF THE WRINKLE BEND. FRONTIER HAD A FAILURE TO PINPOINT AND REPAIR THE LEAK IN 2018 WHEN WE DUG WHERE WE WERE INITIALLY GETTING GAS READINGS. WE DID NOT FIND ANYTHING ON THE TRANSMISSION LINE, THEREFORE WE ASSUME THOSE IN CHARGE AT THE TIME THOUGHT IT HAD TO BE ON OUR PLASTIC DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM LOCATED IN THE SAME VICINITY. THIS SHOULD HAVE BEEN MONITORED AND TRACKED AS A LEAK FROM THIS POINT ON, BUT THAT WAS NOT THE CASE. COMPLIANCE TASKS SUCH AS LEAK SURVEY/VALVE MAINTENANCE FOUND THIS LEAK AGAIN BETWEEN THE YEARS OF 2018-2022, BUT IT WAS STILL ASSUMED TO BE ON THE PLASTIC SYSTEM AND WAS NOT PROPERLY WRITTEN UP BY THOSE IN CHARGE AT THE TIME. HIGH GAS READINGS WERE FOUND DURING 2022 LEAK SURVEY, AND THOSE CURRENTLY IN CHARGE IMMEDIATELY PUT PLANS IN PLACE TO DIG WHERE THE GAS READINGS WERE POINTING US TOWARDS. THE PLEDCO WAS USED IN AUGUST 2022 TO STOP THE LEAK WE FOUND IN THE WRINKLE BEND. THE PLEDCO SHOULDN'T HAVE BEEN USED ACCORDING TO MANUFACTURER'S SPECIFICATIONS, WHICH IS A LESSON LEARNED.  THE PLEDCO FAILED IN JANUARY 2023, AND WE CALLED TDW TO STOPPLE TO REPLACE THE PIPE. THE GAS LOST CALCULATION IN THIS REPORT IS AN ESTIMATE OVER THE 5 YEARS WE ARE AWARE OF THAT THE PIPE WAS LEAKING.

NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 2, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 1206 HOURS, AN FGT TECHNICIAN WAS NOTIFIED BY A DOWNSTREAM CUSTOMER THAT A RELIEF VALVE AT THE CLEARWATER SOUTH REGULATOR STATION WAS CURRENTLY ACTIVATED.  THE CLEARWATER STATION IS SHARED WITH ANOTHER OPERATOR (CLEARWATER GAS COMPANY).  THE FGT TECHNICIAN PROMPTLY RESPONDED TO THE AREA AND ISOLATED THE SOURCE AT APPROXIMATELY 1300 HRS.  LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT AND POLICE RESPONDED TO A 3RD PARTY NOTIFICATION, AND THEY BLOCKED TRAFFIC IN BOTH DIRECTIONS UNTIL THE COMPANY TECHNICIAN ISOLATED THE REGULATOR RUN.  ACCORDING TO SCADA, THE RELIEF VALVE BEGAN VENTING AT APPROXIMATELY 1030 HRS THAT DAY.  THE PRESSURE EXCEEDED THE HI ALARM LIMIT THAT WOULD HAVE INITIATED CLOSER MONITORING BY GAS CONTROL HOWEVER THE PRESSURE DID NOT EXCEED THE HIHI CRITICAL ALARM LIMIT THAT WOULD HAVE GENERATED A CALL OUT AND FIELD INVESTIGATION.         THE VOLUME RELEASED WAS CALCULATED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 3.45 MMSCF NATURAL GAS.  THE DETERMINATION TIME FOR THIS ESTIMATE WAS APPROXIMATELY 1452 HRS.  NRC NOTIFICATION OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 1551 HRS.  THE CLEARWATER SOUTH REGULATOR STATION DOES CONTAIN COVERED SEGMENTS IN THE COMPANY IMP, HOWEVER THE PIPING ASSOCIATED WITH THIS INCIDENT IS NOT A COVERED SEGMENT AS DETERMINED BY METHOD 2 (PIR).    UPON INVESTIGATION THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS CONFIRMED AS A DAMAGED DIAPHRAGM IN A MOODY PILOT ON THE REGULATOR WHICH ALLOWED HIGHER PRESSURE FLOW THROUGH THE STATION WHICH ACTIVATED THE RELIEF VALVE.  THE RELIEF CAPACITY WAS VALIDATED DURING THE RELEASE VOLUME CALCULATION.  THE DAMAGED EQUIPMENT WAS IMMEDIATELY REPLACED BY THE TECHNICIAN.     TO PREVENT RECURRENCE THE COMPANY IS REVIEWING THE HIHI CRITICAL ALARM SETTING AT THIS LOCATION IN RELATION TO RELIEF VALVE SETTING AND WILL RESET THE HIHI ALARM AT A LEVEL BELOW THE RELIEF VALVE SETTING. NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON DECEMBER 30, 2022 AT APPROXIMATELY 01:15 LOCAL TIME, A FIRE OCCURRED AT THE DOMINATOR COMPRESSOR STATION ON UNIT #6, 30 MILES WEST OF JAL, NEW MEXICO IN LEA COUNTY.    OPERATIONS RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE 911 DISPATCHER AND THE FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS DISPATCHED TO THE STATION. THE OPERATIONS MECHANIC, WHO IS ALSO A VOLUNTEER FIRE FIGHTER, ARRIVED WITH THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND ESD'D THE STATION.    A DECISION WAS MADE TO LET THE FIRE BURN ITSELF OUT.    AT 06:00 MOUNTAIN TIME, THE STATION WAS SAFE TO ENTER AND OPERATIONS MADE AN INITIAL ASSESSMENT AND IT WAS DETERMINED THE REPAIRS AND DAMAGES WOULD EXCEED THE $123,900.00 REPORTABLE DOLLAR CRITERIA.    AT APPROXIMATELY 15:30, UNIT #6 WAS ISOLATED AND THE STATION WAS PUT BACK ONLINE BY USING THE OTHER COMPRESSORS.    THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS CALCULATED AT 1500 MCF.    THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION.    COMPONENTS HAS BEEN SENT TO THE LAB FOR ANALYSIS TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE. AND UNIT #6 WILL BE SENT TO THE MANUFACTURER TO BE DISMANTLED AND EXAMINED.    A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE DETERMINATION HAS BEEN MADE.    **3/22/2023 UPDATE**    AFTER THE COMPLETION OF THE LAB ANALYSIS, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE WAS DUE TO A LEAK ON THE COMPRESSOR FUEL RAIL.     THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE FUEL RAIL AND HANDRAIL WERE IN CONTACT FOR SOME PERIOD OF TIME BASED ON THE APPEARANCE OF WEAR ON THE HANDRAIL.  THE HANDRAIL EXPERIENCED VIBRATIONS OVER TIME, EVENTUALLY SHEARING THE BOLT PROVIDED AND INCREASING THE CONTACT BETWEEN THE FUEL RAIL AND HANDRAIL, THUS CAUSING THE FUEL RAIL TO LEAK FUEL GAS AND IGNITE FROM A HEAT SOURCE IN CLOSE PROXIMITY.     TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, OPERATIONS WILL BE VISUALLY INSPECTING, IDENTIFYING, AND CORRECTING UNITS THAT MAY HAVE SIMILAR INSTALLATIONS AND PERFORM PACKAGE ASSESSMENTS DURING ROUTINE PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE.

NARRATIVE: ON 11/28/22 AT APPROX 23:22, TL-442 RUPTURED AT STA 5+00 UNDER AN ACCESS ROAD ON COMPANY PROPERTY IN PINE GROVE, WV. INITIAL NOTICE WAS RECEIVED FROM AN OUTSIDE PARTY AT APPROX 23:23. TL-442 IS A 16 IN OD TRANSMISSION PIPELINE APPROX 0.30 MI LONG AND TRANSPORTS NATURAL GAS FROM HASTINGS CS TO MOCKINGBIRD HILL CS. THE MAOP OF TL-442 IS 990 PSIG. A PRESSURE RESTRICTION OF 960 PSIG WAS ESTABLISHED IN 2003 FOR TL-442 DUE TO ITS CONNECTION TO TL-430 AT HAUGHT JCT. TL-442 WAS IN NORMAL OPERATION WITH AN OP OF 947 PSIG WHEN THE INCIDENT OCCURRED. AT APPROX 23:30, OPS PERSONNEL CALLED 911. ALSO AT APPROX 23:30, THE C-300 UNIT AT HASTINGS CS SHUTDOWN AND THE ASSOCIATED UNIT VALVES CLOSED, ISOLATING TL-442 UPSTREAM OF THE RUPTURE. AT APPROX 23:33, GAS CONTROL REMOTELY CLOSED VALVE-420JJ, ISOLATING TL-442 DOWNSTREAM OF THE RUPTURE. AT APPROX 23:50, OPS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE SITE. THE RUPTURE RESULTED IN AN APPROX 40 FT LENGTH OF PIPE OPENING CIRCUMFERENTIALLY AND LONGITUDINALLY (NOT SEAM ORIENTED) AND BOTH ENDS FOLDING UP AND COMING OUT OF THE GROUND; APPROX 23,403 MCF OF GAS LOSS; DAMAGE TO THE ACCESS ROAD; AND DEBRIS BEING BLOWN ON THE RIGHT-OF-WAY, S.R. 20, AND A RAILROAD. S.R. 20 AND THE RAILROAD WERE TEMPORARILY CLOSED AT 23:40 TO REMOVE DEBRIS. THE GAS DID NOT IGNITE AND THERE WERE NO FIRES, INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR EVACUATIONS. IT WAS DETERMINED ON 11/29/2022 AT 00:44 THAT THE INCIDENT INVOLVED AN UNINTENTIONAL ESTIMATED VOLUME OF GAS LOSS OF 3 MMSCF OR MORE. INITIAL NOTIFICATION (#1353645) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 11/29/22 AT 01:04. FOLLOW UP NOTIFICATION (#1353781) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 11/30/22 AT 11:46 TO CONFIRM THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION AND UPDATE THE CURRENT STATUS OF THE TL-442, THE GPS COORDINATES, THE ESTIMATED VOLUME OF UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS, AND THE TEMPORARY CLOSURE (AND REOPENING) OF S.R. 20 AND THE RAILROAD IN ORDER TO REMOVE DEBRIS. THE ESTIMATED VOLUME OF UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS LATER CONFIRMED TO BE 23,403 MCF. TL-442 WAS RESTARTED ON 12/30/22 AT 14:09 AFTER COMPLETION OF THE FOLLOWING REMEDIATION: APPROX 485 FT OF STATION PIPING AT HASTINGS CS ASSOCIATED WITH TL-442 WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED ALONG WITH VALVE-425D TO RESUME THE FLOW OF GAS BETWEEN HASTINGS CS AND MOCKINGBIRD HILL CS THROUGH TL-597 AND INTO TL-430 WHILE THE REMEDIATION OF TL-442 WAS COMPLETED. BOTH ENDS OF THE PIPE WERE CUT AT THE RUPTURE ON TL-442, UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE HINGED AREAS WHERE THE PIPE FOLDED UP AND CAME OUT OF THE GROUND. THE TWO PIECES OF PIPE THAT WERE CUT-OUT AT THE RUPTURE WERE SENT TO KIEFNER FOR METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS AND REPLACEMENT PIPE WAS INSTALLED. THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS REPORT FROM KIEFNER DETERMINED THAT EXTERNAL CORROSION WHERE DISBONDED POLYETHYLENE COATING WAS SHIELDING CATHODIC PROTECTION WAS THE APPARENT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE. PIPE WAS CUT-OUT AT SELECTED LOCATIONS TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO THE INSIDE OF TL-442 FOR WIRELINE INSPECTIONS. WIRELINES USING CAL AND MFL TOOLS WERE CONDUCTED TO ASSESS THE INTEGRITY OF TL-442 AND REPLACEMENT PIPE WAS INSTALLED AT THE ACCESS LOCATIONS. INITIAL VERIFICATION DIGS WERE COMPLETED ON EITHER SIDE OF THE RUPTURE TO ASSIST IN VALIDATING THE ACCURACY OF THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES. BASED ON THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES, THE RESULTS FROM THE INITIAL VERIFICATION DIGS, AND THE EVALUATION OF ANOMALIES AS DESCRIBED BELOW, APPROX 950 FT OF TL-442 WAS REPLACED. THIS INVOLVED REPLACING TWO SECTIONS OF TL-442, FROM VALVE-425D TO THE SOUTH SIDE OF FISHING CREEK AND FROM THE NORTH SIDE OF S.R. 20 TO MOCKINGBIRD HILL JCT. THE ANOMALIES LOCATED IN THESE TWO SECTIONS WERE EVALUATED AS THE PIPE WAS EXCAVATED PRIOR TO REMOVAL AND FURTHER VERIFIED THE ACCURACY OF THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES. APPROX 120 FT OF TL-442 LOCATED IN A CASING UNDER THE RAILROAD AND S.R. 20 WAS REMOVED AND REPLACEMENT PIPE WAS INSTALLED. AN ANOMALY LOCATED ON THE CASED PIPE THAT WAS REMOVED WAS EVALUATED AND FURTHER VERIFIED THE ACCURACY OF THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES.

RELAY K340-2B DID NOT UNLATCH FROM ITS N/C STATE AFTER LOSING ITS POWER OR DE-ENERGIZED STATE TO N/O WHICH WOULD HAVE ALLOWED UNIT SUCTION/DISCHARGE VALVES TO BECOME CLOSED OR INTO A FAIL TO CLOSE/SHUT PHASE PER DESIGN. NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 9, 2022 OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ON SITE AT THE KEMMERER COMPRESSOR STATION HEARD WHAT APPEARED TO BE A COMPRESSOR RELIEF VALVE RELIEVING GAS. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION THE OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED THE UNIT 1 PSV WAS RELIEVING. IN ORDER TO REMEDY THE SITUATION AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE, THE TECHNICIAN SHUT THE UNIT DOWN, ISOLATED IT FROM PRESSURE, AND BLEW IT DOWN. IT WAS NOTED BY THE TECHNICIAN AT THE TIME THAT THE RELIEF VALVE WOULD NOT RESEAT ITSELF AFTER DECREASING PRESSURE. HMI TRENDS AND STATION CCTV CAMERAS WERE UTILIZED TO TRY AND DETERMINE WHEN THE UNIT STARTED TO RELIEVE, BUT WERE UNSUCCESSFUL IN DETERMINING THE EXACT TIME. AFTER REVIEWING THAT DATA THROUGHOUT THE DAY ON NOVEMBER 9TH AND NOT FINDING A DEFINITIVE ANSWER, IT WAS DECIDED TO CALCULATE A GAS LOSS ESTIMATION FROM THE MOMENT THE OPERATOR ARRIVED ON SITE AT 06:45 TO THE TIME THE UNIT WAS COMPLETELY ISOLATED AND GAS HAD STOPPED RELEASING AT 07:22. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE PILOT ON THIS PSV FAILED DUE TO A HARMONIC FREQUENCY AT THE STATION. IN ORDER TO REMEDY THE SITUATION, OPERATIONS WORKED TO GET A NEW AND DIFFERENT PILOT INSTALLED ON THIS PSV THAT WOULDN'T BE SUSCEPTIBLE TO PREMATURE RELIEVING AS A RESULT OF HARMONICS. NORTHWESTERN (THE LDC) WAS ONSITE AND REPORTED THAT GAS WAS BLOWING.   NORTHERN'S TECHNICIAN ARRIVED ON SCENE AT APPROXIMATELY 21:15 AND FOUND THE RELIEF VALVE RELIVING STACKS HALF OPEN. THE TECHNICIAN CHECKED PRESSURES FROM THE ELECTRONIC FLOW MEASUREMENT (EFM) AND NOTICED THAT NO DISPLAYS WERE WORKING. HE ALSO NOTICED THE EFM WAS NOT BEING POWERED. THE TECHNICIAN CORRECTED THE RELIEF VENTING BY LOWERING THE SET POINT OF THE SECONDARY PNEUMATIC VALVE CONTROLLER.  THE PRIMARY REGULATOR IS CONTROLLED WITH A DIGITAL VALVE CONTROLLER WHICH IS POWERED WITH 24 VOLTS. WHEN THE POWER WAS LOST TO THE DIGITAL VALVE CONTROLLER, THE REGULATOR FAILED OPEN CAUSING THE RELIEF TO VENT DUE TO THE SECONDARY REGULATOR BEING SET SLIGHTLY HIGHER THAN THE RELIEF. IF THE RELIEF WAS SET HIGHER THAN THE SECONDARY REGULATORS, THE RELIEF MAY NOT HAVE OPENED.  ON OCTOBER 3, 2022, FURTHER INVESTIGATION WAS CONDUCTED CONCERNING THE POWER FAILURE TO THE STATION. UPON FURTHER REVIEW OF THE REGULATOR, THIS MODEL REGULATOR HAS A LOW VOLTAGE PROTECT FUNCTION THAT DISCONNECTS ALL THE LOAD ONCE THE BATTERIES REACH 23 VOLTS. NORTHERN NATURAL GAS SETS A LOW VOLTAGE ALARM AT 22 VOLTS. DUE TO THE VOLTAGE REGULATOR DISCONNECTING POWER AT 23 VOLTS, NO ALARMS WERE RECEIVED, NOR COULD ANY OTHER MONITORING BE PERFORMED REMOTELY.

UPDATE:   THE THIRD PARTY FAILURE ANALYSIS REPORT ON THE RUPTURED PIPE SEGMENT INDICATED WITHIN THE PIPE BODY MATERIAL, THERE WERE INTERNAL DEFECTS AND AREAS WITHIN THE MICROSTRUCTURE OF LOW MATERIAL PROPERTIES.  THESE WERE MOST LIKELY DUE TO VINTAGE STEEL MAKING PROCESSES AND PIPE MANUFACTURING METHODS (ESTIMATE PIPE MANUFACTURED IN THE 1940S). OVER THE COURSE OF ALMOST SEVENTY YEARS, THE NORMAL FLUCTUATION IN PIPELINE PRESSURES GREW AND / OR INITIATED INTERNAL CRACKS TO THE POINT THAT THE EFFECTIVE PIPE WALL THICKNESS WAS NOT ENOUGH TO CONTAIN NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURES.  THIS LED TO THE PIPE WALL BULGE THAT CREATED CRACK INITIATION SITES ON THE INTERNAL PIPE SURFACE THAT BECAME CRACKS PROPAGATED BY FATIGUE AND EVENTUALLY LED TO THE PIPE SEGMENT RUPTURE. NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON JULY 28TH, 2022 THERE WAS AN IMPROPER SEALING OF A UNIT VALVE AT NORTHWEST PIPELINE WILLARD COMPRESSOR STATION. WILLIAMS OPERATIONS RECEIVED A CALL FROM SKAMANIA COUNTY 911 DISPATCH AT 22:10 LOCAL TIME REPORTING A STRONG SMELL OF GAS FROM A NEIGHBOR NEAR THE COMPRESSOR STATION. WILLIAMS OPERATIONS PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY RESPONDED TO THE CALL AND ARRIVED ON-SITE AT 23:50 LOCAL TIME TO ASSESS THE SITUATION.     WHILE ON-SITE IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE VENT VALVE ON UNIT ONE AT THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS SHOWING CLOSED ON THE HMI BUT WAS STILL VENTING GAS. IN AN EFFORT TO STOP THE GAS FROM VENTING AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE OPERATIONS TECHNICIANS AT THE SITE CONSULTED WITH PIPELINE CONTROL AND THE OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR AND AGREED TO ISSUE A START COMMAND TO UNIT ONE. ISSUING THIS START COMMAND WAS FOUND TO CAUSE ALL VALVES TO POSITION THEMSELVES CORRECTLY, THUS STOPPING THE GAS FROM VENTING TO THE ATMOSPHERE. SHORTLY AFTER, A STOP COMMAND WAS SUBSEQUENTLY ISSUED TO THE SAME UNIT, WITH OPERATIONS NOTING THAT ALL VALVES ALSO CORRECTLY POSITIONED THEMSELVES AGAIN. IT WAS NOTED BY PIPELINE CONTROL THAT THIS UNIT WOULD NOT BE NEEDED FOR THE REST OF THE NIGHT, SO UNIT ONE WAS LEFT OFF AND UNAVAILABLE UNTIL THE NEXT DAY.     ONCE THE UNIT HAD BEEN SHUT DOWN AND NO ADDITIONAL VENTING WAS CONFIRMED, OPERATIONS CONTACTED THE SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER (SOC) AT 01:40 LOCAL TIME. AT THIS TIME, THE SOC RAN GAS LOSS ESTIMATION CALCULATIONS AND WAS ABLE TO CONFIRM DISCOVERY THAT THE 3MMSCF RELEASE THRESHOLD WAS REACHED. SHORTLY AFTER, AT 01:52, AFTER A CONVERSATION BETWEEN THE SOC AND PIPELINE SAFETY, IT WAS DETERMINED TO REPORT THE INCIDENT TO THE NRC. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL THAT RESPONDED TO THE INCIDENT WENT HOME TO REST BEFORE ARRIVING ON-SITE THE NEXT MORNING TO CONTINUE THE TROUBLESHOOTING PROCESS.     THE FOLLOWING MORNING OPERATIONS AND TECH SERVICES EMPLOYEES WORKED TO TROUBLESHOOT THE VALVE POSITION INDICATORS AND WERE NOT ABLE TO RECREATE THE PROBLEM THAT CAUSED UNIT ONE SUCTION VALVE TO REMAIN CRACKED DURING A REMOTE STOP. TO BETTER ALERT OPERATION PERSONNEL OF A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRING, PIPELINE CONTROL PLACED A TEMPORARY PRESSURE ALARM TO MONITOR CASE PRESSURE. OVER THE COURSE OF THE FOLLOWING WEEKS, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ATTEMPTED TO RECREATE THE ISSUE TO BETTER UNDERSTAND WHAT CAUSED THE INITIAL INCIDENT.     MULTIPLE EFFORTS TO RECREATE THE ISSUE WERE UNSUCCESSFUL AND A FULL ROOT-CAUSE INVESTIGATION HAS SINCE TAKEN PLACE. THE FINDINGS OF THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE UNIT 1 BLOWDOWN VALVE HAD BEEN LEAKING 12 HOURS PRIOR TO PIPELINE CONTROL RECEIVING NOTIFICATION FROM THE EMERGENCY DISPATCH. THE INVESTIGATION INTO WHY THE BLOWDOWN VALVE FAILED TO SEAL FOUND THAT THERE WAS LIKELY SOME DEBRIS IN THE SEAT OF THE UNIT VALVE THAT CAUSED IT TO NOT SEAL PROPERLY. IT'S BELIEVED THAT THESE DEBRIS MAY HAVE ORIGINATED FROM PIPELINE CLEANING / PIGGING EFFORTS AS PART OF A SERIES OF HYDROTEST PROJECTS THAT HAD RECENTLY OCCURRED IN THE AREA. IT WAS ALSO FOUND THAT POWER TURBINE PERCENT SPEED AND SUCTION/DISCHARGE PRESSURES WERE NOT UTILIZED TO SHOW INDICATION OF A POTENTIAL ISSUE WITH THE COMPRESSOR. THESE ITEMS WEREN'T SPECIFICALLY REVIEWED AT THE TIME AS THERE WERE NO ALARMS GIVEN TO PIPELINE CONTROL. TO PREVENT THIS FROM HAPPENING IN THE FUTURE, WILLIAMS IS IMPLEMENTING A CONTINUOUS VENTING UNIT ALARM WITHIN SCADA, STATION, AND UNIT CONTROL SYSTEMS.

NAME: HAYNESVILLE GATHERING LP
NARRATIVE: DURING THE MORNING OF THE INCIDENT, THUNDERSTORMS WERE MOVING THROUGH THE AREA AND THE DOWNSTREAM AMINE TREATMENT PLANT WAS STRUCK BY LIGHTING AND LOST POWER SUBSEQUENTLY SHUTTING IN AT AROUND 08:30. NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC OPERATES AND MAINTAINS CLEMENTSVILLE COMPRESSOR STATION LOCATED IN LIBERTY, KENTUCKY. ON THURSDAY JULY 14TH, 2022 THE MONITORING CENTER CALLED OUT STATION PERSONNEL TO INVESTIGATE THE SHUTDOWN OF 3 COMPRESSOR UNITS AT THE STATION AFTER GAS CONTROL HAD RECEIVED UNIT FAULT INDICATIONS. STATION PERSONNEL ARRIVED ON SITE AND DISCOVERED GAS BLOWING AT THE SIDE GATE OF THE STATION, THEY THEN CHECKED THE HMI CONTROL PANEL AND SAW THE 3 COMPRESSOR UNITS WERE STILL ONLINE AND RUNNING AND PROCEEDED TO SHUT THOSE UNITS DOWN. THE STATION PERSONNEL THEN WENT BACK TO THE HMI TO REVIEW ALARMS AND VALVE MOVEMENTS, AT THAT POINT THE BLOWDOWN HAD STOPPED.    OTHER STATION TECHNICIANS WERE CALLED IN TO ASSIST AND AFTER TROUBLESHOOTING, DISCOVERED A SHORTED CLOSED LIMIT WIRE ON VALVE ACTUATOR 206-1PV. THE SHORTED WIRE TRIPPED A 24VDC BREAKER THAT FEEDS POWER TO DISCRETE I/O MODULES, WHICH ALSO CAUSED THE COMMS TO NOT FUNCTION. AFTER THE REPAIR OF THE SHORTED WIRE ROUTINE SAFETY CHECKS WERE COMPLETED WHICH INCLUDED A CHECK OF THE ESD SYSTEM TO ENSURE SAFETY AND RELIABILITY. ALL ALARMS WERE CLEARED AT THE CONTROL PANEL, FUNCTIONAL TESTS WERE COMPLETED WITH NO NEW ERRORS GENERATED TO ENSURE NORMAL OPERATION OF THE THREE UNITS. AN INVESTIGATION IS STILL UNDERWAY INTO THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE. THE CALCULATED VOLUME OF GAS RELEASED WAS ESTIMATED TO BE 8,072.6 MCF    THE CHRONOLOGY OF EVENTS ON JULY 14TH, 2022 ARE AS FOLLOWS (ALL TIMES WERE RECORDED IN LOCAL CENTRAL DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME):  - 3:17 AM: A  UNIT FAULT INDICATION WAS RECEIVED BY TC GAS CONTROL;  - 3:50 AM: TC OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE SITE AND LOCAL RESPONDERS WERE AT THE SITE;  - 4:04 AM: TC REGULATORY COMPLIANCE MADE A REQUEST FOR VALVE SIZE, PRESSURE, AND TIME OF RELEASE;  - 5:31 AM: TC MONITORING CENTER WAS NOTIFIED OF TOTAL GAS LOST, WHICH AT THE TIME, WAS CALCULATED TO BE 5792.8 MCF BY TC OPERATIONS MANAGER;  - 5:35 AM: TC MONITORING CENTER NOTIFIED TC REGULATORY COMPLIANCE OF TOTAL GAS LOST;  - 5:38 AM: NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER WAS NOTIFIED OF THE INCIDENT;  - 5:45 AM: PHMSA ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION DIVISION WAS NOTIFIED OF THE INCIDENT.    THE DURATION OF THE GAS RELEASE WAS DETERMINED FROM OUR CONTROL SYSTEMS TO BE 29 MINUTES.    INSPECTIONS REVEALED THAT THE MAIN BREAKER POWERING THE REMOTE I/O PANEL THAT CONTROLS VALVE 206-1BD WAS TRIPPED (CB244). FURTHER INVESTIGATION DISCOVERED DAMAGED AND SHORTED WIRING FEEDING VALVE 206-1PV WHICH WAS CONFIRMED TO BE THE CAUSE OF BREAKER CB244 FAULTING.    NOTE REGARDING THE REVISED TIME IN QUESTION A4 ABOVE: IN RESPONSE TO THIS QUESTION THE TIME PROVIDED HERE IS AT THE DIRECTION OF PHMSA AID AND IS NOT AN ADMISSION; WE DID NOT HAVE SUFFICIENT INFORMATION TO DETERMINE WE HAD A REPORTABLE INCIDENT UNTIL 05:31.
